steps: Anchor a band low around a solid post or other object.
Stand with your right side to the post and put your right foot through the band, getting it around the ankle.

Step away from the post until the band has tension, then let your right leg drift out toward the anchor. Stand up straight and hold onto something steady if needed. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the knee straight, pull your right leg across in front of your body toward and slightly past your left leg.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Then switch sides.
Band_Hip_Adductions.note: Rewrote as true adduction (banded leg nearest the anchor, pulled across the body); equipment 'bands' -> 'band'.

steps: Load a barbell with small round plates and kneel on the floor behind it. Grip the bar about shoulder width with your hands directly under your shoulders. This will be your starting position.
Brace your abs, tuck your pelvis slightly, and keep your ribs down so your back stays neutral.
Roll the bar forward away from you, extending your body as far as you can control without letting your lower back sag.
Pull the bar back toward your knees using your abs to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Barbell_Ab_Rollout.note: Replaced the hip-lift/roll-toward-feet pattern and 'slight arch' with a standard kneeling rollout that rolls forward with a braced, neutral spine.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just below shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and step forward with your right leg and squat down through your hips, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes and your whole front foot on the floor.
Push through your front foot and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
Barbell_Lunge.note: Removed knees-past-toes warning and stray 'li>' fragment; cue knee tracking over toes and full-foot drive.

steps: Sit on a bench with back support in a squat rack. Position a barbell at about shoulder height when seated. Grab the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing forward) slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the bar and hold it at the top of your chest, just in front of your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Press the bar straight up overhead until your arms are locked out as you exhale.
Lower the bar back down to the top of your chest slowly as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Barbell_Shoulder_Press.note: Fixed contradictory start: unrack at shoulder level, press to lockout, lower back to the chest.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack to just below shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your whole foot on the floor.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Barbell_Squat.note: Removed knees-past-toes tip and the foot-stances aside; cue knees in line with toes and whole-foot drive.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first place a flat bench or a box behind you. The flat bench is used to teach you to set your hips back and to hit depth.

Then, set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting your hips back as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you slightly touch the bench behind you. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your whole foot on the floor.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Barbell_Squat_To_A_Bench.note: Removed empty step, knees-past-toes tip and foot-stances aside; cue knees in line with toes.

Bench_Press_-_Powerlifting.note: Primary triceps -> chest; triceps moved to secondary. Steps unchanged.

Bench_Press_with_Chains.note: Primary triceps -> chest; triceps moved to secondary. Steps unchanged.

steps: Put weight on one of the ends of an Olympic barbell. Make sure that you either place the other end of the barbell in the corner of two walls; or put a heavy object on the ground so the barbell cannot slide backward.
Straddle the bar facing the loaded end, then bend forward until your torso is as close to parallel with the floor as you can and keep your knees slightly bent.
Grab the bar with both hands just behind the plates, or hook a V-handle under the bar just behind the plates and hold it with both hands. This will be your starting position.

Pull the bar straight up with your elbows in until the plates touch your lower chest. Squeeze the back muscles as you lift the weight up and hold for a second at the top of the movement. Breathe out as you lift the weight.
Slowly lower the bar to the starting position getting a nice stretch on the lats. Do not let the plates touch the floor.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Bent_Over_Two-Arm_Long_Bar_Row.note: Removed the one-arm 'other hand on your knee' line; two-hand grip or V-handle behind the plates; trimmed plate-size aside.

steps: Seat yourself on the bike and adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent when the pedal is at the bottom of the stroke.
Place the balls of your feet on the pedals and hold the handlebars with your torso stable. This will be your starting position.
Pedal at a steady cadence and intensity, pushing down and pulling through the full circle of each stroke.
Continue for the desired time or distance.
Bicycling.note: Added the actual activity: seat height setup, pedaling at a steady cadence, time/distance line.

steps: Stand upright with a kettlebell in one hand, hanging at arm's length in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Hinge at the hips and swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward forcefully and pull the kettlebell up close to your body.
Crush the handle as hard as you can and catch the kettlebell upside down at shoulder height, with the bell above your hand, the base pointing up, and your forearm vertical.
Hold the bell balanced in the bottoms-up position for a moment, then lower it back to the hang position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Then switch sides.
Bottoms-Up_Clean_From_The_Hang_Position.note: Added the defining bottoms-up catch (inverted bell at the shoulder, forearm vertical), the return and the side switch.

steps: Stand in front of a low pulley facing forward with one leg next to the pulley and the other one away.
Attach the ankle cuff to the cable and also to the ankle of the leg that is next to the pulley.
Now step out and away from the stack with a wide stance and grasp the bar of the pulley system.
Stand on the foot that does not have the ankle cuff (the far foot) and allow the leg with the cuff to be pulled towards the low pulley. This will be your starting position.
Now perform the movement by moving the leg with the ankle cuff in front of the far leg by using the inner thighs to adduct the hip. Breathe out during this portion of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then repeat the same movement with the opposite leg.
Cable_Hip_Adduction.note: Primary quadriceps -> adductors; 'abduct the hip' -> 'adduct the hip'.

steps: Place a flat bench between two low pulleys and attach a single handle to each. Select the weight to be used on each pulley.
Sit upright at the end of the bench with your feet flat on the floor, facing so the pulleys are to your left and right.

Grasp the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand so the cables cross in front of you. Your arms should hang by your sides with a slight bend in the elbows and palms facing in. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your torso upright and the slight bend in your elbows fixed, raise your arms out to the sides until they are at shoulder height. Exhale during this movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower your arms to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Cable_Seated_Lateral_Raise.note: Rewrote from a bent-over rear-delt raise to an upright seated crossed-cable lateral raise; fixed 'arms stationary, raise the upper arms'; secondary middle back removed.

steps: Place a heavy hex dumbbell on the floor so that it cannot roll and hold on to a sturdy object for balance.
Stand with the balls of your feet on the dumbbell handle and let your heels drop toward the floor to get a nice stretch in the calves. This will be your starting position.
Raise your heels as high as you can by extending your ankles. Exhale during the execution of this movement. Contract the calves hard at the top and hold for a second.
Slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Calf_Raise_On_A_Dumbbell.note: Removed the deliberately rolling dumbbell; stand on a non-rolling hex dumbbell handle with a support.

Crossover_Reverse_Lunge.note: Primary lower back -> quadriceps (lower back moved to secondary); blank equipment -> body only. Steps unchanged.

Crunch_-_Legs_On_Exercise_Ball.note: Equipment body only -> exercise ball. Steps unchanged.

steps: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip in a standing position. Raise your upper arms out to the sides so that they are parallel to the floor, allowing your lower arms to hang in the "scarecrow" position. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms fixed in place, externally rotate your shoulders about 90 degrees until the forearms are vertical and the wrists are directly above the elbows.
Now press the dumbbells by extending at the elbows, straightening your arms overhead.
Return to the starting position as you breathe in by reversing the steps.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Cuban_Press.note: Fixed step 2: about 90 degrees of external rotation with the upper arms fixed, not 180 degrees of upper-arm movement.

steps: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.

Step forward with your right leg around 2 feet or so from the foot being left stationary behind and lower your upper body down, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes and your whole front foot on the floor.
Push through your front foot and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
Dumbbell_Lunges.note: Removed knees-past-toes warning and vertical-shin rule; cue knee tracking over toes and full-foot drive.

steps: Lie face down on a flat bench holding a light dumbbell by one end in one hand, so the weighted end sticks out above your thumb.
Let the working arm hang off the side of the bench with the upper arm vertical and the elbow bent to 90 degrees, so your forearm points forward parallel to the floor.
Turn your palm to face up so the free end of the dumbbell points out to the side. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the upper arm and elbow still, rotate your forearm to turn your palm in and then down, lifting the free end of the dumbbell up and over.
Slowly rotate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Then switch arms.
Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation.note: Replaced the prone shoulder external rotation with an actual lying forearm pronation (palm up to palm down around a fixed elbow); forearms primary now matches.

steps: Lie face down on a flat bench holding a light dumbbell by one end in one hand, so the weighted end sticks out above your thumb.
Let the working arm hang off the side of the bench, just away from it, with the upper arm vertical and the elbow bent to 90 degrees, so your forearm points forward parallel to the floor.
Turn your palm to face down so the free end of the dumbbell points in toward the bench. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the upper arm and elbow still, rotate your forearm to turn your palm in and then up, lifting the free end of the dumbbell up and over.
Slowly rotate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Then switch arms.
Dumbbell_Lying_Supination.note: Replaced the side-lying shoulder external rotation with an actual lying forearm supination (palm down to palm up around a fixed elbow); forearms primary now matches.

steps: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.

Step backward with your right leg around two feet or so from the left foot and lower your upper body down, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes and your whole front foot on the floor.
Push through your front foot and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
Dumbbell_Rear_Lunge.note: Removed knees-past-toes warning, vertical-shin rule and ball-vs-heel asides; cue knee over toes and full-foot drive.

steps: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).
Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees and hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your whole foot on the floor.
Begin to raise your torso as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Squat.note: Removed knees-past-toes tip and foot-stances aside; cue knees in line with toes and whole-foot drive.

steps: Stand up straight with a flat bench behind you while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).
Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees and hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you slightly touch the bench behind you. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your whole foot on the floor.
Stand up as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Dumbbell_Squat_To_A_Bench.note: Removed knees-past-toes tip and foot-stances aside; 'raise the bar' -> 'stand up'.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain an upright torso with the elbows high. Continue down until the upper legs are below parallel to the floor. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Let your knees travel forward, tracking in line with your toes, with your whole foot on the floor.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor mainly with the middle of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Front_Barbell_Squat.note: Removed knees-past-toes tip and foot-positioning aside; cue forward knee travel in line with toes.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set a flat bench behind you and set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain an upright torso with the elbows high. Continue down until you touch the bench with your glutes. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Let your knees travel forward, tracking in line with your toes, with your whole foot on the floor.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Front_Barbell_Squat_To_A_Bench.note: Removed knees-past-toes tip and foot-positioning aside; cue forward knee travel in line with toes and whole-foot drive.

steps: Begin in a pushup position on the floor. This will be your starting position.
Using both legs, jump forward so your feet land outside your hands in a wide stance, sinking your hips low into a deep squat to open the groin. Keep your head up as you do so.
Jump your feet back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Groiners.note: Feet now land outside the hands in a wide, deep squat (defining groiner detail) instead of next to the hands.

steps: Place the back of your torso against the back pad of the machine and hook your shoulders under the shoulder pads provided.
Position your legs in the platform using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and your back on the pad at all times.
Place your arms on the side handles of the machine and disengage the safety bars (which on most designs is done by moving the side handles from a facing front position to a diagonal position).
Now straighten your legs without locking the knees. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the unit by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with your back on the pad. Continue down until the upper legs are below parallel to the platform. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Let your knees travel forward, tracking in line with your toes.
Begin to raise the unit as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Hack_Squat.note: Removed knees-behind-toes rule and foot-positioning aside; cue knees tracking with toes and whole-foot drive.

steps: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.
By using your thighs to help you get the dumbbells up, clean the dumbbells one arm at a time so that you can hold them at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, keep the palms of your hands with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Keep your elbows tucked about 30 to 45 degrees from your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now lower the dumbbells slowly beside your chest as you breathe in, keeping the elbows tucked and the palms facing each other.
As you breathe out, push the dumbbells up using your pectoral muscles until your arms are straight. Hold for a second and then start coming down slowly.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the dumbbells back on your thighs and then on the floor.
Hammer_Grip_Incline_DB_Bench_Press.note: Elbows now tucked 30-45 degrees with a neutral grip, lowering beside the chest, instead of flared perpendicular to the torso.

steps: Begin with a shoulder width, double overhand or hook grip, with the bar hanging at the mid thigh position. Your back should be straight and inclined slightly forward. This will be your starting position.
Begin by aggressively extending through the hips, knees and ankles, driving the weight upward. As you do so, shrug your shoulders towards your ears.
As the bar rises, pull yourself under it, whipping your elbows around and forward.
Receive the bar racked on the front of your shoulders with elbows high as you drop into a quarter or front squat.
Immediately recover by driving through your feet, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position.
Lower the bar back to the hang position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Hang_Clean.note: Added the pull under, elbow turnover and front-rack receive so it is a clean, not a high pull.

steps: This drill helps you learn the snatch. Begin by holding a light weight across the back of the shoulders with a wide snatch-width grip. Your feet should be slightly wider than hip width apart with the feet turned out, the same position that you would perform a squat with. This will be your starting position.
Dip with the knees slightly, then pop back up to briefly drive the bar off your back.
Immediately drive yourself underneath the bar, punching it up to locked-out arms overhead as you descend into a full overhead squat.
Stabilize the bar overhead at the bottom, then stand up with it locked out.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Heaving_Snatch_Balance.note: Specified the wide snatch grip and the locked-out overhead squat receive; added the return.

Incline_Bench_Pull.note: Equipment barbell -> dumbbell to match the steps (a dumbbell in each hand). Steps unchanged.

steps: Place an incline bench set to about 30 to 45 degrees between two low pulleys and attach a single handle to each.

Adjust the weight to an appropriate amount, grasp the handles and sit back on the bench with your head and chest up. Your upper arms should be about 45 degrees to the body and the handles beside your upper chest with the elbows bent to about 90 degrees. This will be your starting position.
Press the handles up and together over your upper chest by extending through the elbows. Keep your shoulder blades retracted as you execute the movement.
After pausing at full extension, return to the starting position, keeping tension on the cables.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Incline_Cable_Chest_Press.note: Established the incline bench between low pulleys and an upward pressing path over the upper chest.

steps: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.
By using your thighs to help you get the dumbbells up, clean the dumbbells one arm at a time so that you can hold them at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, keep the palms of your hands with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Keep your elbows tucked about 30 to 45 degrees from your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now lower the dumbbells slowly beside your chest as you breathe in, keeping the elbows tucked and the palms facing each other.
As you breathe out, push the dumbbells up using your pectoral muscles until your arms are straight. Hold for a second and then start coming down slowly.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the dumbbells back on your thighs and then on the floor.
Incline_Dumbbell_Bench_With_Palms_Facing.note: Elbows now tucked 30-45 degrees with a neutral grip, lowering beside the chest, instead of flared perpendicular to the torso.

steps: Hold a dumbbell on each hand and lie on an incline bench that is set to an incline angle of no more than 30 degrees.
Extend your arms above your chest with a slight bend at the elbows and your palms facing each other. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the arms out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping the slight bend in the elbows and the neutral grip, until you feel a stretch in your chest.
As you exhale, bring the dumbbells back up along the same arc to the starting position. The movement happens only at the shoulder joint; the elbows stay fixed.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Incline_Dumbbell_Flyes.note: Removed the wrist twist (belongs to the 'With A Twist' variant); neutral grip throughout a standard fly arc.

steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie on an incline bench that is set to an incline angle of no more than 30 degrees.
Extend your arms above you with a slight bend at the elbows.
Now rotate the wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing you and the pinky sides of the dumbbells are next to each other. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the arms out to the sides in a wide arc while rotating the wrists back so that at the bottom your palms face up toward the ceiling.

As you exhale, bring the dumbbells back up along the same arc, rotating the hands so that the pinky sides come together again at the top. Movement happens only at the shoulders and wrists; the elbows stay fixed.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Incline_Dumbbell_Flyes_-_With_A_Twist.note: Made the palm cue consistent: pinkies together/palms facing you at the top, palms up at the bottom (dropped the conflicting 'palms facing each other').

steps: For this drill you will need two aerobic steps or sturdy low boxes about 6 to 12 inches high.

Place the steps a little wider than shoulder width apart and put one hand on each, with your feet on the floor behind you, so you are in an incline pushup position. This will be your starting position.
Remove your hands from the steps and drop down so your hands land on the floor between them, bending your elbows to absorb the impact.
Immediately push explosively off the floor and bring your hands back up onto the steps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Incline_Push-Up_Depth_Jump.note: Hands, not feet, are now elevated so it is an incline position; drop from the steps to the floor and rebound back up.

Intermediate_Groin_Stretch.note: Primary hamstrings -> adductors; hamstrings as secondary. Steps unchanged.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in. This will be your starting position.
Squat down by bending your hips and knees while you raise the dumbbells straight out in front of you to shoulder height.
At the bottom of the squat, sweep the dumbbells out to your sides at shoulder height so your arms form a T.
Bring the dumbbells back in front of you at shoulder height.
Stand back up as you lower the dumbbells to your sides.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Iron_Cross.note: Wrote steps for the dumbbell iron cross: squat while raising to the front, sweep out to a T, return and stand.

steps: Place a barbell on the floor.
Stand in the middle of the bar length wise.
Bend down by bending at the knees and keeping your back straight and grasp the front of the bar with your right hand. Your palm should be in (neutral grip) facing the left side.

Grasp the rear of the bar with your left hand. The palm of your hand should be in neutral grip alignment (palms facing the right side). Tip: Ensure that your grip is even on the bar. Your torso should be positioned right in the middle of the bar and the distance between your torso and your right hand (which should be at the front) should be the same as the distance between your torso and your left hand (which should be to your back).
Now stand straight up with the weight. Tip: Your feet should be shoulder width apart and your toes slightly pointed out.

Squat down by bending at the knees and keeping your back straight until your upper thighs are parallel with the floor. Keep your back as vertical as possible and your head up, with your knees tracking in line with your toes. Inhale during this portion of the movement.
Now drive yourself back up to the starting position by pushing with the feet. Keep the bar hanging at arm's length; the arms only serve as hooks.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Switch which hand is in front between sets.
Jefferson_Squats.note: Removed knees-past-toes cue (now knees track with toes); added repeat/switch line.

steps: Position your body on the vertical leg raise bench so that your forearms are resting on the pads next to the torso and holding on to the handles. Your arms will be bent at a 90 degree angle.
The torso should be straight with the lower back pressed against the pad of the machine and the legs extended pointing towards the floor. This will be your starting position.
Now as you breathe out, bend your knees and raise them toward your chest, curling your hips up off the pad at the top. Hold the contraction for a second. Do not use any momentum or swinging.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Knee_Hip_Raise_On_Parallel_Bars.note: Step 3 changed from a straight-leg raise to bent-knee raise toward the chest with the hips curling up.

steps: To begin, stand on an exercise band so that tension begins at arm's length. Grasp the handles with your palms facing your thighs. The handles should be resting on the sides of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the handles out to the sides as you exhale, leading with your elbows. Continue to lift the handles until your arms are about parallel to the floor. Keep your wrists neutral or thumbs slightly up, your torso stationary, and pause for a second at the top.
Lower the handles back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Lateral_Raise_-_With_Bands.note: Replaced 'pouring water' thumb-down cue with neutral/thumb-up wrist leading with the elbows; equipment 'bands' -> 'band'.

steps: For this exercise you will need to use a leg extension machine. First choose your weight and sit on the machine with your legs under the pad (feet pointed forward) and the hands holding the side bars. Adjust the pad so that it rests on your lower shins just above your feet and the knee lines up with the machine's pivot. This will be your starting position.
Using your quadriceps, extend your legs to the maximum as you exhale. Ensure that the rest of the body remains stationary on the seat. Pause a second on the contracted position.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position as you inhale, using the machine's full comfortable range.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
Leg_Extensions.note: Removed the knee-over-toes / stop-at-90-degrees warning; use the machine's full comfortable range.

steps: Load the pins to an appropriate weight. Position yourself directly between the handles. Grasp the bottom handles with a comfortable grip, and then lower your hips as you take a breath. Look forward with your head and keep your chest up. This will be your starting position.
Drive through your feet, extending your hips and knees together to stand tall with the handles, keeping your back flat.
Lower the handles under control by pushing your hips back and bending your knees until you return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Leverage_Deadlift.note: Added the missing lift (drive to lockout) and controlled lowering.

Lower_Back_Curl.note: Primary abdominals -> lower back to match the prone spinal extension. Steps unchanged.

steps: Adjust the leg machine to a height that will allow you to get inside it with your knees bent and the thighs slightly below parallel.

Once you select the weight, position yourself inside the machine face up with the knees bent and thighs slightly below parallel to the platform. Your back and your head should be resting on the machine while your shoulders are pressed under the shoulder pads.
Place your hands by the handles and position your feet slightly pointing out at a shoulder width position. This will be your starting position.

While pressing with the balls of the feet as you breathe out, make your whole body erect as you squeeze the quads. Hold the contracted position for a second. Tip: Since you are starting below parallel, you can opt to use your hands to help you up by pressing on your thighs only on the first repetition.

Slowly squat down as you inhale but instead of going all the way down to the starting position, just stop once your thighs are parallel to the platform. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Lying_Machine_Squat.note: Removed knees-past-toes cue; knees track in line with toes.

steps: Lie on your side on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in your top hand. Use your bottom arm to support your head or hold the bench for stability.
Let the top arm hang down in front of your body with the elbow slightly bent and your palm facing down. This will be your starting position.
Raise the dumbbell up and out in an arc until your arm is pointing almost straight up toward the ceiling as you exhale, keeping the slight bend in your elbow. Hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Then switch sides.
Lying_One-Arm_Lateral_Raise.note: Changed from a prone rear-delt raise to the side-lying lateral raise the name describes.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a less-than-shoulder-width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Feet should be around 3-6 inches apart. Keep your head up and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the upper legs are just below parallel to the floor. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Let your knees travel forward, tracking in line with your toes, with your whole foot on the floor.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Narrow_Stance_Squats.note: Removed knees-past-toes tip and the contradictory medium-stance note; whole-foot drive.

steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width with a kettlebell on the floor a little in front of you. Hinge at the hips and grab the handle with one hand. This will be your starting position.
Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping your back flat and your arm straight.
Snap your hips forward forcefully and stand tall, letting the kettlebell swing up to about chest height. Keep the free arm out to the side or by your side.
Let the kettlebell fall back between your legs, hinging at the hips to absorb it, and go straight into the next swing.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Then switch hands.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Swings.note: Wrote steps: one-hand hike, hip snap to chest height, let it fall back between the legs, switch hands.

steps: Pick a dumbbell and place it in one of your hands. Your non lifting hand should be used to grab something steady such as an incline bench press. Lean towards your lifting arm and away from the hand that is gripping the incline bench as this will allow you to keep your balance.
Stand with a straight torso and have the dumbbell by your side at arm's length with the palm of the hand facing you. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the dumbbell to your side with a slight bend on the elbow, leading with the elbow and keeping your wrist neutral or thumb slightly up. Continue to go up until your arm is parallel to the floor. Exhale as you execute this movement and pause for a second at the top.
Lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
One-Arm_Side_Laterals.note: Replaced 'pouring water' thumb-down cue with neutral wrist/thumb slightly up.

steps: Grab a chin-up bar with one hand, palm facing you, and hang at arm's length. Keep your free arm by your side or across your body.
Draw your working shoulder down and back and brace your body to limit rotation. This is your starting position.
Pull your body up with the one arm until your chin clears the bar, driving the elbow down toward your side. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position until your arm is fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Then switch arms.
One_Arm_Chin-Up.note: Removed the towel held by the other hand (that is an assisted progression); free hand off the bar. Primary middle back -> lats.

steps: Set a barbell in a squat rack just below shoulder height and place a flat bench about 2 to 3 feet behind where you will stand.
Step under the bar, place it across the back of your shoulders, and lift it off the rack. Walk to the bench and stand facing away from it.
Reach one foot back and rest your toe on the bench, keeping your front foot planted in front of you. Keep your chest up and your back straight. This will be your starting position.
As you inhale, slowly lower your body by bending your front knee until your thigh is parallel to the floor, letting your front knee track over your toes.
Drive through your front foot and straighten your leg to return to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the movement.
One_Leg_Barbell_Squat.note: Replaced floor-to-chest-to-overhead bar placement with unracking from a squat rack; tidied the descent/ascent wording.

steps: For this movement a wooden floor or similar smooth surface is needed. Lie on your back with your knees bent and a gym towel or slider under each heel.
Lift your hips into a bridge so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your hips up, slide your heels away from you until your legs are almost straight.
Pull your heels back toward your glutes, still keeping your hips raised, to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Platform_Hamstring_Slides.note: Performed from a hip bridge with the hips held up through the slide (both heels), so the hamstrings are loaded.

steps: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length, palms facing your torso. Your feet should be about shoulder width apart.
Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are about 45 degrees from your body. This will be your starting position.
Explosively raise the dumbbells the rest of the way to shoulder height, keeping the slight bend in your elbows and your wrists neutral.
Lower the dumbbells only back to the 45-degree starting position and immediately go into the next rep.
Continue with fast, continuous partial reps for the desired number of repetitions.
Power_Partials.note: Added the defining short top-range explosive partials; removed the pinky-up cue.

steps: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands slightly wider than shoulder width apart, holding your torso up at arms length.
Place your toes on top of a flat bench. This will allow your body to be elevated. Note: The higher the elevation of the flat bench, the higher the resistance of the exercise is.
Lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
Using your pectoral muscles, press your upper body back up to the starting position and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you perform this step.
After a second pause at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Push-Ups_With_Feet_Elevated.note: Hand width 36 inches -> slightly wider than shoulder width.

steps: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands slightly wider than shoulder width apart, holding your torso up at arms length.
Place your toes on top of an exercise ball. This will allow your body to be elevated.
Lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
Using your pectoral muscles, press your upper body back up to the starting position and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you perform this step.
After a second pause at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Push-Ups_With_Feet_On_An_Exercise_Ball.note: Hand width 36 inches -> slightly wider than shoulder width.

steps: Hold a barbell in the front rack position across the front of your shoulders with a grip just outside shoulder width, elbows slightly in front of the bar. Stand with your feet about hip width apart. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your torso upright, dip by bending your knees a few inches.
Drive up forcefully through your legs and use that momentum to press the bar straight overhead.
Finish by locking out your arms with the bar over the middle of your feet.
Lower the bar back to the front rack position, bending your knees slightly to absorb it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Push_Press.note: Wrote steps: front rack, short vertical dip, leg drive into an overhead press to lockout, return.

steps: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands slightly wider than shoulder width apart while holding your torso up at arms length.
Next, lower yourself downward until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
Now breathe out and press your upper body back up to the starting position while squeezing your chest.
After a brief pause at the top contracted position, you can begin to lower yourself downward again for as many repetitions as needed.
Pushups.note: Hand width 36 inches -> slightly wider than shoulder width.

Rear_Leg_Raises.note: Primary quadriceps -> glutes; hamstrings as secondary. Steps unchanged.

steps: Set a barbell in a rack at about mid-thigh height, or deadlift it from the floor. Grip it with a pronated (palms facing down) grip a little wider than shoulder width and stand up straight with the bar at arm's length. This will be your starting position.
Unlock your knees slightly and keep them at that bend throughout the movement.
Push your hips back and lower the bar along your thighs, keeping your back neutral and the bar close to your legs, until it is just below your knees or at mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to return to the standing position, without letting the bar touch the floor between reps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Romanian_Deadlift.note: Starts standing, defines the bottom at just below the knee/mid-shin, no floor reset between reps.

steps: Stand on a raised platform or a stack of plates about 2 to 4 inches high, holding a bar at arm's length in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Unlock your knees slightly, then push your hips back as far as possible, lowering the bar along your legs with a neutral spine.
Continue lowering the bar past the level of the platform toward your feet as far as your hamstring flexibility allows.
Drive your hips forward to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Romanian_Deadlift_from_Deficit.note: Made the deficit platform required and the bar travels below platform level; added repeat line.

steps: Hold an end of the rope in each hand with the rope behind you on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Turn the rope over your head with your wrists, keeping your elbows close to your sides, and bring it down in front of you.
When the rope reaches the ground, hop over it with small, quick bounces on the balls of your feet.
Find a turning pace that you can maintain, and continue for the desired time.
Rope_Jumping.note: Primary quadriceps -> calves (quads to secondary); split the instructions into steps and dropped the calorie aside.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet together, holding a bodybar or broomstick in front of your hips with a wide, overhand grip.
Keeping your elbows straight, slowly raise the stick in front of you and up overhead.
Continue the circle, bringing the stick back behind you until it reaches your hips or as far as you comfortably can. Widen your grip if needed.
Return the stick along the same path to the front of your hips.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Round_The_World_Shoulder_Stretch.note: Rewrote as the stick pass-through from the front of the hips, overhead, to behind the hips and back.

steps: Sit on a military press bench with the bar racked in front of you at about shoulder height. Grip it with a pronated grip (palms facing forward) just outside shoulder width.
Unrack the bar and hold it at your collarbone. This is your starting position.
Press the bar straight overhead until your arms are locked out as you exhale.
Lower the bar back down to the collarbone slowly as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Seated_Barbell_Military_Press.note: Fixed contradictory start: bar unracked in front at the collarbone, pressed to lockout, lowered to the collarbone.

steps: Stand up straight with your arms relaxed at your sides. This will be your starting position.
Raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can and hold for a moment.
Lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Shoulder_Raise.note: Primary shoulders -> traps, removed lats secondary, blank equipment -> body only; expanded to setup/move/return steps.

steps: Stand or sit up straight and reach your left arm across your chest, keeping it straight.
Place your right hand on your left arm just above the elbow.
Gently pull the arm in toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the back of your shoulder.
Hold for the desired time, then switch sides.
Shoulder_Stretch.note: Added the pull with the opposite hand, the hold and the side switch; blank equipment -> body only.

steps: Lie on your side with your forearm on the floor directly under your shoulder and your feet stacked. This will be your starting position.
Lift your hips off the floor so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold this position, keeping your hips from sagging.
Hold for the desired time, then switch sides.
Side_Bridge.note: Wrote steps for the forearm side bridge hold with side switch.

steps: Lie on your right side with your legs stacked and your knees slightly bent. Place your left hand behind your head and your right forearm on the floor for support. This will be your starting position.
Raise your top leg while crunching your upper torso sideways, bringing your left elbow and left knee toward each other.
Squeeze your obliques at the top, then lower your leg and torso back to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Side_Jackknife.note: Wrote steps (none existed): side-lying, top leg and torso crunch together, switch sides.

steps: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing in. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights out to your sides to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
At the top, keep the weights at shoulder height and sweep them horizontally around to the front of your body.
Lower the weights from the front back to your sides with a controlled motion.
On the next repetition, raise the weights in front of you to shoulder height, sweep them horizontally out to your sides, and lower them from the sides.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the direction of the sweep each rep.
Side_Laterals_to_Front_Raise.note: First rep now raises laterally and sweeps to the front; second rep reverses, as the name and old step 5 intended.

steps: Position a bar into a landmine or securely anchor it in a corner. Load the bar to an appropriate weight.
Raise the end of the bar from the floor and hold it at your shoulder with one hand. Adopt a wide stance. This will be your starting position.
Dip slightly at the hips and knees, then explosively extend your hips, knees and ankles as you press the bar up and forward with that one arm until your elbow is locked out.
Lower the bar back to your shoulder under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Single-Arm_Linear_Jammer.note: Made it explicitly one-armed: bar held at one shoulder, single-arm press driven by the hips and knees, switch sides.

steps: Position a high box in a rack. Secure a band or rope in place above the box.
Stand on one leg with your back to the box, holding the band for balance, with your other leg held off the floor in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Sit back and down on your working leg until your glutes lightly touch the box.
Drive through your working foot to stand back up without putting the other foot down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
Single-Leg_High_Box_Squat.note: Replaced the step-up with a single-leg squat down to a high box (box and band setup kept).

steps: Place an incline bench underneath the smith machine. Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down with your arms fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the incline bench and make sure your shoulders are aligned right under the barbell.
Using a shoulder width pronated (palms forward) grip, lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your elbows locked.
Keeping your elbows locked, let your shoulder blades pull back together so the bar lowers a few inches. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe out, push the bar up by pushing your shoulders forward, raising your shoulder blades off the bench. Keep your arms straight the whole time.
After a second pause, let your shoulder blades pull back together to lower the bar to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then return the bar to the rack.
Smith_Incline_Shoulder_Raise.note: Changed the press to a locked-arm shoulder blade protraction and set equipment to machine (Smith), matching the other Smith rows.

steps: Adjust the barbell on the smith machine to fit your height and align a raised platform right under the bar.
Stand on the platform with the heels of your feet secured on top of it with the balls of your feet extending off it. Position your toes facing forward with a shoulder width stance.

Now, place your shoulders under the barbell while maintaining the foot positioning described and push the barbell up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is standing erect. The knees should be kept with a slight bend; never locked. This will be your starting position. Tip: The barbell on your back is only for balance purposes.

Pull your toes up toward your shins as high as possible as you breathe out, keeping your heels on the platform. Keep your knees still throughout. Hold the top position for a second before you start to go back down.
Slowly go back down to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering the balls of your feet and toes.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises.note: Changed step 4 from 'flex your calf' to pulling the toes up toward the shins. Primary stays calves because tibialis anterior is not an allowed muscle and calves is the closest lower-leg option.

steps: To begin, first set the bar on the height that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side (palms facing forward), unlock it and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up, keeping your knees tracking in line with your toes. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Smith_Machine_Squat.note: Removed the outdated knees-behind-toes rule (knees now track in line with the toes) and the reference to a foot stances section that doesn't exist.

steps: To begin, place a flat bench 2-3 feet behind the smith machine. Then, set the bar on the height that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side (palms facing forward), unlock it and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
Position your legs by placing one foot slightly forward under the bar and extending your other leg back and place the top of your foot on the bench. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knee as you maintain a straight posture with the head up, keeping your front knee tracking over your toes with the whole foot planted. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calf becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten your leg again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
Smith_Single-Leg_Split_Squat.note: Removed the outdated knees-behind-toes rule; front knee now tracks over the toes with the foot planted. Merged the repeat and switch-legs steps.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up, keeping your knees tracking over your toes. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.

Begin to raise the bar as fast as possible without involving momentum as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position. Note: You should perform these exercises as fast as possible but without breaking perfect form and without involving momentum.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Speed_Squats.note: Removed the outdated knees-behind-toes rule (knees track over the toes) and the reference to a foot stances section that doesn't exist.

steps: Stand in a staggered stance with one foot about two to three feet in front of the other, your back heel raised and your torso upright. This will be your starting position.
Bend both knees to lower your back knee toward the floor, keeping your front foot flat.
Stop just before your back knee touches the floor, then drive through your front foot to rise back up without jumping or moving your feet.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
Split_Squats.note: Replaced the jumping split (switch lunge) with a static split squat. Primary changed to quadriceps (hamstrings dropped to secondary), and the blank equipment set to body only.

steps: Start by placing a barbell that is about chest high on a squat rack. Once you have selected the weights, grab the barbell using a pronated (palms facing forward) grip slightly wider than shoulder width.

Slightly bend the knees and place the barbell on your collar bone. Lift the barbell off the rack keeping it resting on your chest. Take a step back and position your feet shoulder width apart. This is your starting position.
Press the bar straight up overhead as you exhale, moving your head back slightly to let the bar pass, then bring your head forward under the bar as you lock out your arms.
Lower the bar back down to the collarbone slowly as you inhale.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Standing_Military_Press.note: Fixed the self-contradictory start position: the press now starts at the collarbone, goes to overhead lockout with the head moving through, and lowers back to the collarbone.

steps: Secure a set of suspension straps with the handles hanging about a foot off of the ground. Move yourself into a pushup plank position facing away from the rack.
Place your feet into the handles. You should maintain a straight posture, not allowing the hips to sag. This will be your starting position.
Begin the movement by flexing the knees and hips, drawing the knees to your torso. As you do so, posteriorly tilt (tuck) your pelvis, rounding your lower back.
At the top of the controlled motion, return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Suspended_Reverse_Crunch.note: Changed the cue to a posterior (tucked) pelvic tilt and added the repeat step.

steps: Suspend your straps at around chest height. Take a handle in each hand and lean back. Keep your body erect and your head and chest up. Your arms should be fully extended. This will be your starting position.
Begin by flexing the elbows to pull your chest toward the handles, retracting (squeezing) your shoulder blades as you do so.
At the completion of the motion pause, and then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Suspended_Row.note: Changed 'protract' to retracting the shoulder blades and added the repeat step.

steps: Stand upright with your feet at shoulder width and rise up onto the balls of your feet with your heels raised. Use one hand to hold onto the beams of a squat rack and the opposite arm to hold a plate on top of your chest. This is your starting position.

As you use one arm to hold yourself, lean your torso back as you drive your knees forward and down, keeping a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Inhale as you go down and stop when your upper and lower legs almost create a 90-degree angle. Hold the stretch position for a second.
After your one second hold, use your thigh muscles to bring your torso back up to the starting position. Exhale as you move up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Weighted_Sissy_Squat.note: Start position now has the heels raised (on the balls of the feet), with a lean back as the knees drive forward. Equipment barbell changed to other (plate).

steps: Start by positioning two flat benches shoulder width apart from each other. Stand on top of them and wrap the weighted belt around your waist with the amount of weight you feel comfortable with. Make sure your toes are facing out.
Once you are standing straight up with the weight hanging in between your legs, position your arms so that they are fully extended to the side of your body. This is the starting position.

Begin by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up, keeping your knees tracking over your toes. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.

Begin to move the body back up by pushing through your whole foot into the bench as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Weighted_Squat.note: Removed the outdated knees-behind-toes rule; you now drive through the whole foot instead of the ball of the foot.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a wider-than-shoulder-width stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance, and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up, pushing your knees out over your toes. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Wide_Stance_Barbell_Squat.note: Removed the outdated knees-behind-toes rule; knees are now pushed out over the toes.

steps: This is a multi-part stretch. Begin by lunging forward, with your front foot flat on the ground and on the toes of your back foot. With your knees bent, squat down until your back knee is almost touching the ground. Keep your torso erect, and hold this position for 10-20 seconds.
Now, place the hand opposite your front leg on the ground, and drop the elbow on the same side as your front leg down next to the instep of your front foot. Hold for 10-20 seconds.
Rotate your torso toward your front leg and reach that same arm up toward the ceiling, following your hand with your eyes. Hold for 10-20 seconds.

Place your hands on either side of your front foot. Raise the toes of the front foot off of the ground, and straighten your leg. You may need to reposition your rear leg to do so. Hold for 10-20 seconds.
Return to the lunge, then repeat the entire sequence on the other side.
Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.note: Added the defining thoracic rotation (reach to the ceiling after the elbow drops to the instep) and set the blank equipment to body only.

steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. The correct height should be anywhere above the waist but below the chest. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, lock your hands together and place the bar on top of your arms in between the forearm and upper arm.
Lift the bar up so that it is resting on top of your forearms. If you are holding the bar properly, it should look as if you have your arms crossed but with a bar running across them.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up, keeping your knees tracking over your toes. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing through your whole foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Zercher_Squats.note: Removed the outdated knees-behind-toes rule; you now drive through the whole foot instead of the ball of the foot. Also dropped the reference to a foot stances section that doesn't exist.

steps: Position yourself sideways on a 45-degree hyperextension bench with your hip on the pad and your feet secured under the ankle pads. Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head, with your body in a straight line. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your body facing forward, slowly lower your torso sideways toward the floor.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then raise your torso back up to the starting position using your obliques.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0002.note: Changed the plain standing side bend to a side-lying side bend on a 45-degree hyperextension bench, with a switch-sides step. Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Attach a handle to each high pulley (or use a pulldown station with independent handles) and sit or kneel facing the machine with your back straight.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, arms fully extended overhead. This will be your starting position.
Pull one handle down to the side of your chest, driving your elbow down toward your hip, while the other arm stays extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return the handle to the starting position.
Repeat the pull with the other arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating arms.
yd-0007.note: Made it alternate: one handle is pulled down at a time while the other arm stays extended.

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you, with a partner standing in front of you.
Engage your core and lift your knees towards your chest, keeping your legs together.
Have your partner push your knees forcefully down toward the floor.
Resist and brake the descent before your legs reach the bottom, without letting them swing, then bring your knees back up to your chest with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0010.note: Added the partner who throws the legs down; you now brake and raise them again with control instead of throwing them yourself and letting them swing.

steps: Position yourself in a vertical knee raise station (captain's chair) with your forearms on the arm pads, your hands on the grips and your back against the back pad, legs hanging straight down.
Engage your core muscles and lift your knees towards your chest, bending at the hips and knees.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your abs.
Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0011.note: Supplied the assistance: forearm and back support on a vertical knee raise station instead of a dead hang.

steps: Lie flat on your back with a partner standing behind your head and grasp your partner's ankles.
Engage your abs and raise your straight legs, keeping them together, until they are vertical. This will be your starting position.
Have your partner push your legs down and to one side.
Resist the push and stop your legs before they touch the floor, then raise them back to vertical.
On the next repetition your partner pushes your legs toward the other side.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating sides.
yd-0012.note: Added the partner's lateral push down; you resist, stop short of the floor and return, alternating sides.

steps: Lie flat on your back with a partner standing behind your head and grasp your partner's ankles.
Engage your core and raise your straight legs until they are perpendicular to the ground. This will be your starting position.
Have your partner push your legs forcefully down toward the floor.
Resist the push and stop your legs before they touch the floor, then raise them back to vertical.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0013.note: Fixed the contradictory steps 5 and 6 and added the partner's push down; you resist and return to vertical.

steps: Select the counterweight on the assisted pull-up machine and kneel (or stand) on the assistance pad.
Grasp the parallel handles with a close grip, palms facing each other, with your arms fully extended. This will be your starting position.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the handles, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0015.note: You now kneel or stand on the counterweighted pad instead of hanging free. Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Lie face down on a mat or bench with your legs fully extended, with a partner holding your ankles (or a resistance band looped around them).
Engage your hamstrings and curl your heels towards your glutes by bending your knees against the resistance.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position as the resistance pulls against you.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0016.note: Changed the impossible straight-knee lift to a prone leg curl (knee flexion) against a partner or band. Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Select the counterweight on the assisted pull-up machine and kneel (or stand) on the assistance pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with your arms fully extended. This will be your starting position.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the handles, driving your elbows down toward your sides.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0017.note: You now kneel or stand on the assistance pad instead of hanging free. Replaced the elbows-close cue with elbows driving down to the sides.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ends of a towel with both hands behind your head, with a partner standing behind you holding the middle of the towel.
Keep your elbows close to your ears and your upper arms stationary.
Extend your forearms upward against your partner's downward pull on the towel, squeezing your triceps at the top.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the towel back down to the starting position as your partner keeps pulling down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0018.note: Added the resistance: a partner pulls down on the towel during both the extension and the lowering.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the ground.
Hold the barbell with a shoulder-width pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, lower the barbell behind your head in an arc until you feel a stretch in your lats.
Pull the barbell back over your chest in the same arc, then bend your elbows to lower it to your lower chest.
Press the barbell back up to lockout above your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0022.note: Added the press: after the pullover the bar comes down to the chest and is pressed to lockout.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a short fixed-weight barbell in each hand at its center, palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms stationary and exhale as you curl one bar while contracting your biceps, keeping the other arm extended.
Continue to raise the bar until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale as you slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, then curl with the other arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating arms.
yd-0023.note: Kept barbell (it's in the name) and specified short fixed-weight barbells, one per hand. The arms now clearly alternate.

steps: Stand in front of a flat bench with your feet shoulder-width apart and the barbell resting on your upper chest, just below your collarbone.
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, keeping your elbows up and your upper arms parallel to the ground. This will be your starting position.
Lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, keeping your torso upright and your chest up, until your glutes lightly touch the bench.
Without relaxing on the bench, drive through your feet to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0024.note: Added the bench: you front squat until your glutes lightly touch it, then drive up.

steps: Set up a barbell on a squat rack at shoulder height and place a flat bench behind where you will stand.
Step under the bar, place it across your upper back and grasp it with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lift the barbell off the rack and step back until the bench is just behind you, with your feet shoulder-width apart. This will be your starting position.
Lower your body into a squat, keeping your knees in line with your toes and your chest up, until your glutes lightly touch the bench.
Pause for a moment, then push through your feet to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0026.note: Bar now set at shoulder height and unracked before squatting, and the squat goes down to touch the bench.

steps: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and the barbell resting on your front shoulders in a clean grip, fingertips under the bar and elbows pointing forward and high.
Lower your body by bending your knees and hips, sitting straight down between your heels.
Keep your chest up, your torso upright and your elbows high as you lower down, letting your knees travel forward over your toes as needed.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to stand back up, extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0029.note: Replaced the knees-behind-toes cue with forward knee travel and an upright torso, and spelled out the clean-grip rack. Primary changed to quadriceps for a front squat (glutes moved to secondary).

steps: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your feet, holding a barbell with a close grip at arm's length above your chest.
Lower the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
From there, let your elbows drop toward your sides and bring the bar down to your lower chest.
Press the barbell back up to lockout with your close grip.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0035.note: Added the close-grip press phase after the skull crusher lowering.

steps: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, about 1.5 times shoulder-width or more.
Lower the barbell to your chest, keeping your elbows out to the sides.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0036.note: The grip is now clearly wide (about 1.5x shoulder width or more).

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of your thighs.
