Pull your elbows back as you curl, keeping the bar in contact with your torso as it slides up to your lower chest.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell down your torso the same way to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0038.note: Changed to a true drag curl: the elbows travel back and the bar stays on the torso.

steps: Lie on a flat bench with your feet on the ground, holding a barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip resting on your thighs with your arms straight.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the barbell in an arc until it is over your chest.
Continue the arc, lowering the barbell behind your head until your arms are in line with your torso and you feel a stretch.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the arc back over your chest and down to your thighs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0040.note: Moved the exercise onto a bench as one continuous arc (front raise from the thighs into a pullover behind the head), then reversed.

steps: Straddle a barbell on the floor with a wide stance, the bar between your feet running front to back, toes turned slightly out.
Squat down and grip the center of the bar with one hand in front of your body and the other hand behind it, back flat and chest up. This will be your starting position.
Drive through your feet and stand up, lifting the bar between your legs while keeping your torso upright.
Squat back down under control, lowering the bar until it nearly touches the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch which hand and foot is in front.
yd-0051.note: Changed to a true Jefferson squat: you straddle the bar with one hand in front and one behind, then switch sides.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the barbell with a close grip, about shoulder-width or slightly narrower, and hold it at arm's length over your chest.
Lower the bar toward your chin and upper chest by bending your elbows, letting them travel forward while pointing toward your feet.
Stop a few inches above your upper chest, then extend your elbows to press the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0052.note: Changed the regular bench press to a JM press: close grip, bar lowered toward the chin with the elbows forward, then extended.

steps: Lie face down on a high flat or incline bench with your shoulders at the end and your upper arms resting against the end of the pad, holding a barbell with an underhand grip at full arm extension.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0059.note: Changed the seated preacher setup to lying face down with the upper arms supported over the end of the bench.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart or closer and your toes pointing forward.
Hold the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps or rear delts.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you slowly lower your body by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0063.note: Stance is now narrow (hip-width or closer, toes forward). Primary changed to quadriceps, since a narrow stance is quad-dominant.

steps: Stand over a barbell with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over your midfoot.
Squat down and grip the center of the bar with one hand using an overhand grip, with your back flat, chest up and your free arm out for balance. This will be your starting position.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, pulling the bar up close to your body.
As the bar rises past your chest, pull yourself under it, rotate your elbow under the bar and punch it to lockout overhead in one movement, catching it in a partial squat.
Stand up fully with the bar locked out overhead.
Lower the barbell back down to the floor in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0067.note: Grip changed to one hand at the center of the bar, with the free arm out for balance and a single pull straight to overhead lockout.

steps: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, resting it on your chest.
Engaging your abs, sit up until your torso is upright, pressing the barbell from your chest to straight arms overhead as you rise.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower the bar back to your chest as you lower your upper body to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0071.note: Added the press: the bar goes from the chest to overhead as you sit up and comes back down as you lower.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with a wide overhand grip, palms facing down.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight and letting the bar hang at arm's length.
Flare your elbows out to the sides and raise the bar toward your upper chest, keeping your upper arms at about 90 degrees to your torso and squeezing your rear delts.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0075.note: Replaced the impossible straight-arm raise to the sides with a wide-grip, elbows-flared bent-over raise to the upper chest.

steps: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, resting it on the front of your shoulders. This will be your starting position.
Press the bar up just high enough to clear the top of your head, then lower it behind your neck.
Press it back up just over your head and lower it to the front of your shoulders.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating front and back without locking out.
yd-0087.note: Changed to a true Bradford press: the bar alternates between the front of the shoulders and behind the neck, just clearing the head, with no lockout.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart with a barbell across your upper back, holding it with both hands.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Slowly bend your torso directly to the right side, bending only at the waist.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the left side.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating sides.
yd-0096.note: Moved the bar to the upper back and made the bend a straight sideways one.

steps: Place a flat bench behind you, hold a barbell across your upper back and reach one foot back to rest its top on the bench, with your front foot planted about two feet ahead. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your torso upright, lower your body by bending your front knee and letting your back knee drop toward the floor.
Continue lowering until your front thigh is about parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push through your front foot to rise, staying in the split stance.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-0099.note: The back knee now bends and you stay in the split stance. I also put the rear foot on a bench (the single-leg version, matching Smith_Single-Leg_Split_Squat), which the flag didn't ask for.

steps: Load a light weight, around 50-60% of your one-rep max, and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Hold the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps or rear delts.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lower your hips back and down under control.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Drive up as fast as possible to stand back up, accelerating through the whole rep.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0101.note: Added the speed: a light load (about 50-60% 1RM), controlled descent and maximal-speed drive up. Primary changed to quadriceps to match Speed_Squats.

steps: Kneel on a padded mat with your knees hip-width apart and a barbell across your upper back, taken from a low rack setting, gripping it with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Start tall on your knees with your hips fully extended and your torso upright. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your back straight, sit your hips back toward your heels.
Drive your hips forward to return to upright, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0102.note: Changed to a hips-back-to-heels kneeling squat with a forward hip drive. Primary changed to glutes because the move is mainly hip extension; calves dropped from secondary.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell behind your back at arm's length, hands shoulder-width apart and palms facing backward.
Let your wrists relax so the bar hangs down toward your fingers.
Keeping your arms still, curl your wrists up toward your forearms as far as possible.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0104.note: Bar is now held behind the back, palms facing back, with the wrists curled up. Removed biceps and shoulders from secondary because a wrist curl doesn't work them.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell in front of your shoulders with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. This will be your starting position.
Press the bar up just high enough to clear the top of your head, then lower it behind your neck.
Press it back up just over your head and lower it to the front of your shoulders.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating front and back without locking out.
yd-0105.note: Changed to a true Bradford press: the bar alternates front to behind the neck, just clearing the head, with no lockout.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary.
Exhale and curl the weights, bringing the barbell as close to your shoulders as possible while keeping your palms facing down.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0110.note: Grip changed to overhand (pronated), which is what makes it a reverse curl.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hold a barbell across your upper back.
Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, balancing on the balls of your feet.
Lower your heels and keep rocking back onto them, lifting your toes off the floor.
Rock forward again and rise straight back up onto the balls of your feet, moving in a continuous rocking motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0111.note: Added the rocking: back onto the heels with the toes lifted, then forward onto the balls of the feet.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell across your upper back with both hands.
Engage your core and keep your back straight, with your feet planted and hips square throughout the exercise.
Slowly rotate your torso to the right, turning only your upper body.
Pause for a moment at the end of the twist, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat the twist to the left side.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating sides.
yd-0112.note: Moved the bar to the upper back and fixed the contradiction: feet stay planted and hips square while only the torso rotates.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing forward, and hands about shoulder-width apart.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up, until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Pull the barbell towards your lower ribs, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0118.note: Grip changed to underhand (supinated) at shoulder width. The bar now pulls to the lower ribs with the elbows close.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, about 1.5 to 2 times shoulder-width, with your index fingers on or outside the rings.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows flared out.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest, then push it back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0122.note: The grip is now clearly wide (1.5-2x shoulder width).

steps: Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge next to your hips.
Slide your butt off the bench with your knees bent about 90 degrees and your feet flat on the floor in front of you.
Bend your elbows and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your back close to the bench.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0129.note: Knees now bent about 90 degrees with the feet flat, instead of straight legs.

steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips at the end and your legs hanging toward the floor, gripping the bench for support.
Keeping your legs straight, squeeze your glutes and raise your legs until they are in line with your torso.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0130.note: Replaced the incoherent setup with a prone bench hip extension (straight legs raised to hip height).

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands close together, a few inches apart.
Engage your core and pull yourself up towards the bar, focusing on using your biceps to lift your body.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0139.note: Grip narrowed to a few inches apart, palms facing you.

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull yourself up by bending your elbows, bringing your chest towards the bar.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0140.note: Grip changed to underhand (palms facing you) to match the biceps-focused name and primary.

steps: Attach a handle to each high pulley of a cable crossover and stand in the middle facing away from the machine, in a staggered stance.
Hold a handle in each hand behind your head with your elbows bent and your upper arms beside your head. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, extend one arm overhead and forward until it is straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating arms.
yd-0149.note: Now faces away from high pulleys and extends overhead and forward against the cable, alternating arms.

steps: Place a flat bench between the two low pulleys of a cable crossover and attach a handle to each.
Lie on the bench holding a handle in each hand at chest level, elbows bent and below the bench. This will be your starting position.
Press the handles straight up over your chest until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the handles back to chest level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0151.note: Changed the standing cable chest press to a press lying on a bench between low pulleys.

steps: Attach a handle to each high pulley of a cable crossover machine.
Kneel or stand in the middle of the machine and grasp the handles with an overhand grip, arms extended up and out. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your chest up, pull the handles down and in toward the sides of your chest, driving your elbows down to your sides.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0153.note: Pulleys now set high so the handles can actually be pulled down and in.

steps: Set both pulleys of a cable crossover to the high position and attach a handle to each.
Hold a handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance, leaning slightly forward with your arms out to your sides and elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.
Sweep your hands down and together in front of your lower chest or hips, keeping the bend in your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0158.note: Replaced the meaningless 'decline position' with a high-to-low cable fly path.

steps: Attach a wide straight bar to a low pulley and sit on the floor facing the machine with your feet braced and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the bar with a wide overhand grip, palms facing down, arms fully extended and back straight. This will be your starting position.
Pull the bar towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0160.note: You now sit facing the low pulley and use a wide straight bar instead of a single handle.

steps: Place an incline bench set to about 45 degrees in front of a cable crossover and attach a handle to each low pulley.
Sit on the bench facing away from the machine, holding a handle in each hand at shoulder height. This will be your starting position.
Press the handles up and forward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0169.note: Changed to low pulleys behind the bench with you facing away, so the press works against the cable.

steps: Set the pulleys of a cable machine to the lowest position and place a stability ball between them.
Grasp a handle in each hand and sit on the ball, then walk your feet forward until your upper back and shoulders rest on the ball with your hips slightly lower, giving an incline position.
Start with your arms out to the sides at chest level, palms facing up and a slight bend in your elbows.
Keeping the elbow angle fixed, sweep your arms up and together in an arc until your hands meet over your upper chest.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your arms back out to the sides to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0170.note: Rewrote: reclined on the ball with low pulleys, flying the hands up and together over the upper chest.

steps: Attach the handles to the low pulleys of a cable machine and select an appropriate weight.
Stand in the middle of the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Grasp the handles with your palms facing forward, arms down and slightly out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows, feeling a stretch in your chest.
Keeping the elbow angle fixed, sweep your arms forward and upward in an arc until your hands meet in front of your upper chest.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your chest muscles.
Slowly reverse the motion and lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0179.note: Rewrote the path so the hands sweep up from low pulleys to upper-chest height; stretch moved to the bottom, squeeze at the top.

steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands close together.
Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the bar towards your chest by contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0182.note: Step 3: hands close together instead of shoulder-width.

steps: Attach a rope to the low pulley of a cable machine and place a flat bench in front of it.
Lie face up on the bench with your head towards the machine and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the rope with both hands behind your head, elbows bent and pointing up and back.
Pull the rope up and over your head by bringing your elbows forward towards your chest.
As the rope passes over your face, extend your elbows to finish with your arms straight above your chest.
Reverse the motion, bending your elbows and lowering the rope back behind your head.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0184.note: Rewrote: low pulley behind the head, bent-elbow pullover finishing with an elbow extension above the chest.

steps: Stand side-on to a low pulley cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with the hand farthest from the machine so the cable runs across the front of your body.
Bend forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
With a slight bend in your elbow, raise your arm out to the side until it is in line with your torso.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your arm back across your body to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0191.note: Primary changed to shoulders (rear delts); rewrote as a cross-body low-pulley bent-over lateral raise.

steps: Stand side-on to a low pulley cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with the hand farthest from the machine so the cable crosses in front of your body.
With a slight bend in your elbow, raise your arm out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0192.note: Rewrote setup: side-on to a low pulley, handle in the far hand, cable crossing in front of the body.

steps: Attach a rope to the low pulley of a cable machine and stand facing away from it with the rope running between your legs.
Grasp the rope with both hands between your thighs and walk forward to create tension in the cable, feet shoulder-width apart.
With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at the hips and push them back, letting the rope travel back between your legs until your torso is nearly parallel to the ground.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand up tall, keeping your arms straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0196.note: Added the low pulley and rope between the legs; hinge back with hands between the thighs, then drive hips forward.

steps: Attach a stirrup handle to a cable pulley set at chest height and stand facing the machine.
Grasp the handle with your left hand, palm facing down, and step back until your arm is extended in front of you with tension on the cable.
Stand tall with your knees slightly bent and your core engaged.
Pull the handle towards your left shoulder, keeping your elbow flared out to the side at about 90 degrees from your torso.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your rear delt and shoulder blade.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0202.note: Rewrote: pulley at chest height, elbow flared about 90 degrees, pulling the handle toward the shoulder.

steps: Attach a rope to a cable pulley set at chest to face height.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and step back to create tension in the cable.
Grasp the rope with an overhand grip, arms extended in front of you.
Pull the rope towards your face, flaring your elbows out wide to the sides at shoulder height.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your rear delts and shoulder blades.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0203.note: Rewrote: pulley at chest/face height, elbows flared wide, pulling the rope toward the face.

steps: Attach a handle to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grasp the handle in one hand, step back, and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Bring your upper arm in line with your torso, tucked against your side, with your elbow bent about 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arm still, extend your elbow and drive the handle back until your arm is straight.
Pause, then slowly bend your elbow to return the handle.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0204.note: Rewrote as an elbow extension against the cable (the old steps were a curl); triceps primary kept. Revised again after the second review.

steps: Attach a wide bar to the high pulley of a lat pulldown station.
Sit facing the machine with your feet flat on the ground and your thighs secured under the pads.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your torso upright and tilt your head slightly forward.
Pull the bar down behind your head to the base of your neck, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly let the bar rise back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0205.note: Rewrote to pull the bar behind the head to the base of the neck.

steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine and place a preacher bench in front of it.
Sit at the preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, palms facing down and hands shoulder-width apart, with your elbows fully extended.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar towards your shoulders, keeping your palms facing down.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0209.note: Fixed the grip to overhand, palms down throughout; cleaned up the setup.

steps: Set a cable pulley to elbow height and sit on a bench side-on to the machine.
Grasp the handle with the hand nearest the machine.
Keep your elbow tucked against your side and bent at 90 degrees, with your forearm pointing towards the machine.
Keeping your elbow at your side, rotate your forearm inward across your stomach.
Pause for a moment, then slowly rotate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0216.note: Rewrote: side-on, elbow bent 90 degrees at the side, rotating the forearm across the stomach.

steps: Place a Bosu ball beside a low pulley cable machine with the dome facing up.
Stand on the dome with your feet hip-width apart and grasp the handle with the hand nearest the machine.
Place your other hand on your hip.
Keeping your back straight, slowly bend sideways towards the machine.
Crunch your obliques to bend back past upright, away from the machine.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0221.note: Added the Bosu ball (standing on the dome) and the low-pulley setup.

steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the bar behind your back with your arms extended and your palms facing back.
Keep your arms straight and still.
Slowly curl your wrists upward, raising the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0224.note: Rewrote: facing away from a low pulley, bar held behind the back, palms facing back.

steps: Set the pulleys on both sides of a cable crossover machine to the highest position.
Stand in the middle of the machine and grasp the left cable with your right hand and the right cable with your left hand, so the cables cross in front of you.
Start with your arms extended in front of you at shoulder height, hands crossed and a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment when your arms are in line with your body, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0225.note: Rewrote as a true reverse fly with high crossed pulleys, pulling out and back.

steps: Attach a handle to the low pulley of a cable machine and stand facing away from it.
Grasp the handle with your right hand and raise your upper arm overhead so it is beside your ear.
Keep your upper arm stationary and your elbow pointing up.
Slowly bend your elbow, lowering the handle behind your head.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then extend your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and perform the exercise with your left arm.
yd-0231.note: Rewrote: facing away from a low pulley, upper arm overhead by the ear, lowering behind the head.

steps: Attach a rope to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
Grasp the rope with both hands, arms extended in front of you with a slight bend in your elbows.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, pull the rope down towards your thighs, squeezing your lats.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly release the rope back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0232.note: Primary changed to lats; cue squeezing the lats with arms nearly straight instead of the biceps.

steps: Attach a rope to a cable pulley set at face height.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, grasp the rope with an overhand grip, and step back to create tension in the cable.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged, arms extended in front of you.
Pull the rope towards your face, flaring your elbows out wide to the sides at shoulder height.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your rear delts and shoulder blades, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0233.note: Added face-height pulley and wide flared elbows pulling toward the face.

steps: Set a cable pulley to elbow height and stand side-on to the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with the hand farthest from the machine.
Tuck your elbow against your side and bend it to 90 degrees, with your forearm across your stomach.
Keeping your elbow at your side, rotate your forearm outward, away from your body.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0235.note: Rewrote: side-on, elbow bent 90 degrees at the side, cable from the opposite side, rotating outward.

steps: Set the pulleys on both sides of a cable crossover machine to the highest position and place a flat bench between them.
Lie face up on the bench and grasp the left cable with your right hand and the right cable with your left hand.
Start with your arms extended above your chest, hands crossed and a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull your arms down and out to the sides in a wide arc until they are level with your torso.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return your arms to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0240.note: Rewrote supine (face up) with crossed high pulleys, pulling the arms down and out.

steps: Attach ankle straps to a low pulley and lie face up on a mat with your feet towards the machine.
Secure the straps around your ankles and place your arms at your sides, palms down.
Bend your knees to 90 degrees with your thighs vertical.
Curl your knees towards your chest, lifting your hips off the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips and legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0242.note: Moved the cable to the ankles; the hands no longer hold it.

steps: Set a cable pulley to chest height and stand side-on to the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the handle with both hands in front of your chest, keeping your arms slightly bent.
Engage your core and rotate your torso away from the machine, pulling the cable across your body.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, feeling the contraction in your abs and obliques.
Slowly return to the starting position, resisting the cable's pull.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0243.note: Rewrote setup to stand side-on to a chest-height pulley, rotating away from the machine.

steps: Place a cambered bar on the floor under a high flat bench.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and your head just past the end.
Reach down and grab the cambered bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar up towards the bench, squeezing your shoulder blades together and letting the camber clear the bench.
Pause for a moment, then lower the bar until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0248.note: Kept chest support on a high bench and added the cambered bar rowed up to the bench.

steps: Hang from close parallel handles with your palms facing each other.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the handles, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0253.note: Grip fixed to neutral (palms facing each other); primary changed to lats.

steps: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Lie back on the ball until your lower back is supported and your upper body is parallel to the floor.
Extend both arms straight overhead in line with your torso.
Engage your abs and lift your upper body off the ball, curling your shoulders towards your hips while keeping your arms straight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0272.note: Step 3: arms extended straight in line with the torso throughout.

steps: Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your hips, arms extended and palms facing up.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, sweep the dumbbells out to the sides and overhead in a wide semicircle until they meet behind your head.
Reverse the arc, sweeping the dumbbells back out to the sides and down to your hips.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0288.note: Rewrote as the 'around' variant: dumbbells sweep in a wide semicircle from the hips to overhead and back.

steps: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Sit upright against the back support and raise the dumbbells to shoulder height beside your ears, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0290.note: Rewrote as an upright seated shoulder press from shoulder height, not lowered to the chest.

steps: Stand in front of a bench, facing away from it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands.
Bend at the knees and hips to lower yourself down towards the bench, keeping your chest up and back straight.
Once your glutes touch the bench, push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0291.note: The dumbbell is now held at the chest (goblet) throughout.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your palms facing you.
Pull the dumbbells up in an upright row until your elbows are at shoulder height and bent to 90 degrees.
Keeping your elbows in place, rotate your forearms up and back until they are vertical and the dumbbells are beside your head.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Reverse the sequence: lower to the rotated position, rotate your forearms down, then lower the dumbbells to your thighs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0299.note: Rewrote with the upright row, external rotation and press phases.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your thumbs pointing forward.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
With your thumbs up, raise your arms about 30 degrees forward of your sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until they reach shoulder height.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0311.note: Added thumbs-up grip and raising in the scapular plane, about 30 degrees forward.

steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your palms facing each other throughout.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the weights until the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0313.note: Removed the palm rotation; the grip stays neutral throughout.

steps: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
Rotate your arms outward so your palms face forward and angle your arms slightly out to the sides.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbells out towards the outsides of your shoulders.
Continue until your biceps are fully contracted.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0322.note: Added the outward-rotated arms and curling the dumbbells out toward the sides of the shoulders.

steps: Set an incline bench to a moderate angle and lie on your side against it, holding a dumbbell in your top hand.
Let the dumbbell hang in front of your body with your palm facing down and a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is about vertical.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-0323.note: Rewrote: side-lying on an incline bench, raising the top arm out to the side.

yd-0330.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Raise the dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Keeping them at shoulder height, sweep the dumbbells out to the sides until your body forms a T shape.
Sweep the dumbbells back to the front, then lower them to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0332.note: Rewrote as a front raise sweeping out to the sides and back.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and extend your arm straight up above your shoulder.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, bend your elbow and lower the dumbbell across your face towards the opposite shoulder.
Pause for a moment, then extend your elbow to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0337.note: Rewrote as one-arm, lowering across the face toward the opposite shoulder.

steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with your knees just past the end.
Hold a dumbbell securely between your feet with your legs extended.
Curl your heels towards your glutes, keeping your hips pressed into the bench.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0339.note: Rewrote as a prone leg curl with the dumbbell between the feet.

steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down.
Let your arm hang straight down towards the floor with a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is level with your torso, squeezing your rear delt.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0341.note: Changed the raise to go out to the side (rear delt), not up and back.

steps: Kneel or sit beside a flat bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your thumbs up.
Rest your forearms on the bench with your hands just past the edge.
Keeping your forearms flat on the bench, raise the dumbbells by bending only at the wrists.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0365.note: Rewrote as a thumbs-up wrist movement only; primary changed to forearms.

steps: Kneel or sit beside a flat bench and hold a dumbbell in one hand with your thumb up.
Rest your forearm on the bench with your hand just past the edge.
Keeping your forearm flat on the bench, raise the dumbbell by bending only at the wrist.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0366.note: Rewrote as a thumbs-up wrist movement only; primary changed to forearms.

steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up.
Rest your forearm on the bench with your wrist hanging off the edge.
Slowly curl your wrist upwards, bringing the dumbbell towards your forearm.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-0367.note: Step 1: palm up instead of palm down; removed shoulders/biceps as secondary.

steps: Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Rest your upper arms on the pad with your arms extended and your palms facing each other.
Keeping your upper arms on the pad, exhale and curl the dumbbells up with your palms facing each other.
Continue until the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0370.note: Rewrote on a preacher bench with a neutral (hammer) grip throughout.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
As you reach the bottom of the squat, explode upward, jumping straight up off the ground.
Land softly in the same shoulder-width stance and sink straight into the next squat.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0371.note: Removed the mid-air foot switch; jump straight up and land in the same stance.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing back.
Bend forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight, arms hanging down.
Row the dumbbells up with your elbows flared out to the sides at about 90 degrees from your torso.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your rear delts, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0377.note: Rewrote as a bent-elbow row with elbows flared about 90 degrees.

steps: Set an incline bench at a low angle and stand behind it with a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward and rest your forehead on the top of the bench, letting your arms hang down.
Raise your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until they are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0379.note: Added the forehead resting on a bench.

steps: Sit on a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad and your chest against the support.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and your palms facing down, exhale and curl the dumbbells up.
Continue until the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0384.note: Grip changed to overhand, palms down throughout.

steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists just past your knees.
Keeping your forearms still, raise the dumbbells by bending only at the wrists.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0397.note: Rewrote as a wrist-only neutral-grip movement; primary changed to forearms.

steps: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Lean your torso forward, keeping your back straight.
Pin your upper arm alongside your torso with your elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arm still, extend your elbow until your arm is straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your elbow back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0398.note: Added upper arm pinned to the torso at 90 degrees, extending only at the elbow.

steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down.
Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
Keeping your upper arm stationary and your palm facing down, exhale and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder.
Pause for a moment at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0403.note: Grip changed to overhand, palm down throughout.

steps: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inward.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing each other.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead, keeping your palms facing each other.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0404.note: Kept the neutral grip at the shoulders and throughout the press.

steps: Stand on one foot on the edge of a step or platform with your heel hanging off, lifting your other foot off the step.
Hold a dumbbell in the same-side hand and place your other hand on a wall or railing for support.
Raise your heel as high as possible, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down below the step.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
yd-0409.note: Made it single-leg: standing on one foot with the dumbbell in the same-side hand.

steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing forward.
Bend forward at the hips and place your free hand on your thigh for support, letting the working arm hang straight down.
Keeping your upper arm vertical and stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0418.note: Rewrote bent over with the arm hanging vertically and a palm-up grip.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Pin your upper arms beside your torso with your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arms still, extend your elbows until your arms are straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your elbows back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0420.note: Added upper arms pinned beside the torso at 90 degrees, extending only at the elbows.

steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing forward.
Bend forward at the hips and place your free hand on your thigh for support, letting the working arm hang straight down.
Keeping your upper arm vertical and stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0421.note: Rewrote bent over with the working arm hanging vertically.

steps: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended over your chest and palms facing your feet.
Let the inner ends of the dumbbells touch.
Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows outward to lower the dumbbells to your chest.
Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0436.note: Rewrote as a lying Tate press with elbows flaring out.

steps: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Raise the dumbbells beside your shoulders with your elbows tucked low and close to your ribs, forearms angled out to form a W.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Lower the dumbbells back to the W position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0438.note: Added the W start with elbows tucked low against the ribs.

steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate your palms to face forward.
Curl the dumbbells up to your shoulders while keeping your upper arms stationary.
At the top of the movement, rotate your wrists so that your palms face down.
Slowly lower the dumbbells all the way down with your palms facing down.
At the bottom, rotate your palms back to face forward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0439.note: Lowering is now done palms down, rotating back only at the bottom.

steps: Lie face down on an incline bench, holding an ez barbell with an overhand grip.
Raise the bar to shoulder level in front of your head, elbows bent.
Press the bar forward and overhead in line with your torso until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0445.note: Rewrote as a prone incline-bench press in line with the torso.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ez barbell on the inner handles with an underhand grip, hands narrower than shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0446.note: Step 1: inner handles, hands narrower than shoulder width.

steps: Lie on a decline bench with your head lower than your feet.
Grasp the ez barbell on the inner handles with a close overhand grip.
Extend your arms straight up above your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Lower the barbell towards your face by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then press the barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0448.note: Step 2: close overhand grip on the inner handles; lower toward the face.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the ez barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width or closer.
Lower the bar towards your chin and upper chest by bending your elbows and letting them travel forward, keeping your forearms angled.
Press the bar back up to the starting position by extending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0450.note: Rewrote as a JM press: close grip, elbows forward, lowering toward the chin/upper chest.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ez barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Curl the barbell upwards while exhaling.
Continue to raise the barbell until it is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Slowly bring the barbell back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0451.note: Grip changed to overhand, palms down.

steps: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the ez barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Rest your upper arms on the pad, allowing your forearms to hang down.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0452.note: Grip changed to overhand, palms down.

steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip.
Let your arms hang straight down towards the floor.
Keeping your upper arms vertical and stationary, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0454.note: Rewrote chest-down on an incline bench with the arms hanging vertically.

steps: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight up over your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower until your upper arms touch the floor, feeling a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0458.note: A barbell fly is impossible; rewrote as a dumbbell floor fly and changed equipment. The '(with Barbell)' name still needs a rename or removal. A fly cannot be done with a barbell; renamed to the dumbbell version the steps describe.
yd-0458.name: Dumbbell Floor Fly

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull your body up towards the bar while drawing your knees up to your chest.
Continue until your chin is above the bar and your knees are at chest height.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body and legs back down together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0467.note: Rewrote as a chin-up combined with a knee raise to the chest.

steps: Lie flat on your back with the soles of your feet pressed together and your knees falling out to the sides.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Keeping your soles together and knees open, engage your abs and curl your head and shoulders off the ground toward your knees.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0469.note: Replaced the generic reverse crunch with the butterfly-position crunch (soles together, knees out).

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.
Engage your core and lift your straight legs up in front of you until they are parallel to the ground.
Continue by curling your hips up and rolling your pelvis back, bringing your legs toward the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips and legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0474.note: Added the hip-curl phase past parallel that distinguishes the hip raise from a leg raise.

steps: Lie on an incline bench with your head at the high end, your back flat against the bench and your legs extended straight.
Grip the top of the bench behind your head for support.
Engaging your abs, lift your straight legs off the bench until they point toward the ceiling.
Continue by curling your hips off the bench, bringing your legs toward your head.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips and legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0491.note: Added the hip-raise phase and set the incline bench orientation and grip.

steps: Kneel on the end of a bench with your ankles secured under a pad or held by a partner.
Keep your body straight from your knees to your head, with your hands in front of your chest.
Keeping your hips extended, slowly lower your torso forward by straightening at the knees, resisting with your hamstrings.
Lower as far as you can control.
Curl your body back up to the starting position by contracting your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0496.note: Replaced the unloaded prone leg curl with the kneeling Nordic-style inverse leg curl on a bench.

steps: Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body into a squat position, placing your hands on the ground in front of you.
Kick your feet back, landing in a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, lowering your chest to the ground and then pushing back up.
Jump your feet forward, landing in a squat position.
Stand up and perform a jumping jack, jumping your feet out wide as you swing your arms overhead, then jumping them back together.
Land softly and immediately lower back into the squat position to begin the next repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0501.note: Replaced the vertical jump with a jumping jack at the top of each rep.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at arm's length with your palms facing your body.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight, so the kettlebells hang just above your knees.
Explosively extend your hips and knees and pull one kettlebell up close to your body, keeping the other one hanging.
Rotate your hand around the handle and catch the kettlebell in the rack position, resting on the outside of your forearm with your elbow tucked against your ribs.
Lower the kettlebell back to the hang position under control.
Clean the other kettlebell the same way, alternating arms each repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0518.note: Made it a true one-bell-at-a-time alternating hang clean to the rack; primary forearms -> glutes.

steps: Clean a kettlebell to the rack position in your right hand, with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and toes turned slightly to the left.
Press your right elbow against your side so your forearm stays vertical under the kettlebell.
Shift your hips to the right and lean your torso to the left and forward, sliding your left hand down the inside of your left leg while your right arm stays vertical.
Keep your eyes on the kettlebell as you continue lowering your torso away and under it until your right arm is fully locked out.
With the arm locked, stand back up so the kettlebell is held overhead.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0524.note: Replaced the windmill pattern with a bent press: arm stays fixed while the torso lowers under the bell from the rack.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand with an overhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Allow the kettlebell to hang down between your legs, with your arm fully extended.
In one fluid motion, explosively extend your hips and knees while pulling the kettlebell up towards your shoulder.
As the kettlebell rises, crush the handle hard and keep your wrist straight so the bell flips bottom-up.
Catch the kettlebell upside down in front of your shoulder, forearm vertical, palm facing in and elbow tucked, holding it balanced.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position by reversing the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0525.note: Added the crush-grip bottoms-up catch with vertical forearm; primary biceps -> forearms.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand at your chest, with your upper arm on the floor and your forearm vertical.
Press the kettlebell straight up towards the ceiling until your elbow is locked and your wrist is straight.
At the top, reach the kettlebell further toward the ceiling by lifting your shoulder blade off the floor.
Let your shoulder blade settle back to the floor, then slowly lower the kettlebell until your elbow touches the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-0531.note: Added the lowering phase to the floor and the extra range at the top (shoulder blade reach); used scapular reach instead of the flag's bridge idea.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Clean the kettlebell(s) to the rack position, resting on the outside of your forearms with your elbows tucked close to your body.
Engage your core and keep your torso upright as you lower your hips down and back, as if sitting into a chair.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0533.note: Changed the goblet hold to the kettlebell rack position.

steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips, then lift your knees an inch off the floor.
Lift your left hand and rotate your body to the left, kicking your right leg through under your body and out to the left side.
Extend your right leg fully, supporting yourself on your right hand and left foot with your hips low.
Pull the leg back under your body and return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, kicking your left leg through and lifting your right hand.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0555.note: Replaced the seated leg extension with the kick-through/sit-out from a beast hover; primary hamstrings -> abdominals.

steps: Adjust the leverage machine to your desired resistance level.
Kneel on the assist pad and grip the handles with an underhand grip, about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended, keeping your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the handles, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0572.note: Changed to an underhand shoulder-width grip and kneeling on the assist pad.

steps: Stand on the foot platform of the lever row machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hinge forward at the hips with your back straight and chest up, resting your chest on the pad if the machine has one.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
Pull the handles towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0574.note: Converted the free barbell row to a lever machine row; equipment barbell -> leverage machine.

steps: Adjust the machine and stand between the lever arms.
Bend your elbows and place your forearms under the pads, keeping your hands relaxed and not gripping.
Keeping your back straight, exhale and elevate your shoulders as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a brief moment, then inhale and slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0580.note: Removed the handle grip; load goes through the forearm pads with relaxed hands.

steps: Stand on the foot platform of the lever row machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hinge forward at the hips with your back straight, bracing your free hand on the pad or your thigh.
Grip a single handle with one hand, arm fully extended.
Pull the handle up towards your lower chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade toward your spine at the top of the movement.
Lower the handle back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0589.note: Converted the two-hand barbell row to a one-arm lever machine row; equipment barbell -> leverage machine.

steps: Adjust the leverage machine to fit your body.
Lie face down with your torso on the pad, your hips at the edge and your legs hanging down.
Hook your ankles under the lever pad and grip the handles.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to lift your legs upward until they are in line with your torso.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0593.note: Fixed setup to torso on the pad with legs hanging, so the legs do the work.

steps: Adjust the seat height and chest pad position according to your comfort.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor or under the foot rollers.
Grasp the handles or side bars for stability.
Engage your abs and crunch forward, rounding your trunk to push the chest pad down.
Pause for a moment at the maximum contraction, feeling the tension in your abs.
Slowly return to the upright starting position, resisting the weight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0595.note: Reversed the direction so the working phase is forward trunk flexion against the chest pad.

steps: Adjust the machine to fit your body and sit on it with your back against the backrest.
Rest the back of your lower legs, just above your ankles, on the padded lever and lock the thigh pad down on your thighs.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine for support.
Keeping your upper legs stationary, exhale and curl the pad down and back under the seat as far as possible.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your hamstrings.
Inhale and slowly let the lever return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0599.note: Fixed pad placement and curl direction for a seated (not lying) curl.

steps: Grab the pull-up bar with one hand overhand and the other underhand, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, switching which hand is underhand on the next set.
yd-0627.note: Changed to a mixed grip (one over, one under) and added switching hands between sets.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a neutral-grip (Swiss) Olympic bar by the parallel handles.
Let the bar hang at arm's length in front of your thighs, with your palms facing each other.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0636.note: Changed to a neutral grip on a Swiss/football Olympic bar; kept the name and equipment rather than renaming.

yd-0642.note: Steps are correct; primary glutes -> chest and secondary updated for a push-up variation.

steps: Start in a high plank with your hands on the floor under your shoulders and your shins resting on the stability ball.
Brace your abs and keep your body in a straight line from head to ankles.
Pull your knees toward your chest, rolling the ball in toward your hands.
Pause for a moment, then slowly extend your legs, rolling the ball back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0650.note: Replaced seated-on-ball setup with the plank knee tuck, shins on the ball.

steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
As you push back up, drive one leg under your body toward the opposite side, rotating your hips slightly.
Bring the leg back to the starting position and repeat the push-up, then switch to the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0661.note: Changed the side kick to a kick under and across the body; primary glutes -> chest.

steps: Start in a high plank position with both hands together on top of the medicine ball.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the ball by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0663.note: Fixed hand placement to both hands together on the one ball.

steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Push back up to the starting position, using your chest muscles to lift your body.
At the top, raise one arm straight out in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your hips square.
Return the hand to the floor and repeat the push-up, then raise the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0666.note: Moved the arm raise to the top of a full two-hand push-up and alternated arms.

steps: Grab the pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Tilt your head slightly forward and pull your body up so the bar passes behind your head, keeping your elbows pointing out to the sides.
Continue pulling until the bar reaches the base of your neck.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0670.note: Changed the finish to behind the neck, elbows out.

steps: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands behind you gripping the edge, fingers pointing forward.
Walk your feet out with your legs extended, slide your hips off the bench and straighten your arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0672.note: Replaced the parallel-bar dip with the hands-behind bench dip.

steps: Step onto the treadmill and start the belt at a walking pace.
Set the speed and incline you want to run at.
Run with a natural stride, landing lightly under your hips and keeping your arms relaxed.
Stay near the middle of the belt with your posture upright.
Run for the desired time or distance, then slow to a walk before stopping the belt.
yd-0684.note: Rewrote as a treadmill run; 'treadmill' isn't an allowed equipment value, so set 'machine'.

steps: Start by standing upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Keep your upper body relaxed and lean slightly forward from the ankles.
Begin running forward with a natural stride, landing lightly on your midfoot under your hips.
Swing your arms in a relaxed motion with your elbows bent at about 90 degrees.
Maintain a steady pace for the desired time or distance.
yd-0685.note: Replaced running in place with high knees by forward running with a natural stride.

steps: Sit on the edge of a chair with your feet flat on the ground, slightly wider than hip-width.
Place your hands on your thighs.
Slowly round your spine forward, letting your chest drop toward your thighs and your hands slide toward the floor.
Let your head hang and hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling it in your lower back.
Slowly roll back up to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0690.note: Let the spine round instead of keeping a flat-back hinge; primary lats -> lower back.

steps: Kneel on a pad on the floor with your ankles anchored under a fixed object or held by a partner.
Keep your body straight from your knees to your head, with your hands in front of your chest.
Keeping your hips extended, slowly lower your torso toward the floor, resisting with your hamstrings.
When you can no longer control the descent, catch yourself with your hands on the floor.
Push off the floor with your hands just enough to help start the movement, then curl back up to the starting position with your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0696.note: Replaced the bridge with a floor Nordic curl, using a hand push-off to assist.

steps: Kneel on a pad facing a bench or box, with your ankles anchored under a fixed object or held by a partner.
Keep your body straight from your knees to your head, with your hands ready over the bench.
Keeping your hips extended, slowly lower your torso forward, resisting with your hamstrings and using your hands on the bench to control the descent.
Pause just above the bench.
Push with your hands as little as needed while you curl back up to the starting position with your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0697.note: Replaced the supine knee tuck with a Nordic curl assisted by hands on a bench.

steps: Stand between two parallel bars with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place your hands on the bars and lift your body off the ground, supporting your weight on straight arms with your legs hanging.
Engage your abs and raise your knees up and toward one side, twisting your hips so your knees travel toward one shoulder.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat toward the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0709.note: Changed the blocked side leg lift to an oblique knee raise toward each shoulder; kept abdominals (obliques isn't an allowed value).

steps: Start by lying on your side with your legs extended and stacked on top of each other.
Wrap your bottom arm across your waist and place your top hand on the floor in front of your chest, fingers pointing toward your head.
Press through your top hand to straighten that arm, lifting your upper body off the floor while your hips and legs stay down.
Lower your upper body back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0717.note: Replaced the side plank lift with a side-lying push-up pressed through the top hand.

steps: Place a dumbbell (a hex dumbbell lying flat works best) on the floor next to a wall or sturdy support.
Stand with the ball of one foot on the dumbbell and your heel hanging lower, holding the support with one hand.
Lift your other foot off the ground and let your heel drop as low as possible.
Slowly raise your heel as high as possible, using your calf muscles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down below the dumbbell.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
yd-0727.note: Stood on the dumbbell for the deficit instead of only holding it.

steps: Adjust the sled machine to a comfortable weight and position yourself with your back against the pad.
Place your feet close together on the platform, hip-width apart or narrower, with your toes pointing forward.
Grip the handles on the sides of the machine for stability.
Engage your core and slowly lower your body by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your feet to extend your legs and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0741.note: Set a close stance; primary glutes -> quadriceps.

steps: Set the Smith bar at about mid-thigh height and stand with your back to it, feet shoulder-width apart.
Reach behind you and grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar by rotating it, and hold it with straight arms behind your thighs.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top.
Hold for a moment, then lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0746.note: Moved the bar behind the thighs, facing away from the Smith bar.

steps: Place an upright bench under the Smith machine so the bar travels just behind your head, and set the bar at about head height.
Sit with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, wider than shoulder-width apart.
Press the bar up slightly and rotate it to unhook it from the rack.
Lower the bar under control behind your head to about ear level, keeping your elbows pointing out to the sides.
Press the bar up overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down behind your head.
