Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0747.note: Made it seated under the Smith bar, unracked by rotating, with no step-back and elbows out to the sides.

steps: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and step under it, resting it across your upper back and gripping it overhand.
Unhook the bar by rotating it.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart, about a foot in front of the bar.
Keep your chest up and sit back and down as if into a chair, leaning back into the bar with your shins close to vertical.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0750.note: Set feet forward of the bar and sat back to chair depth with near-vertical shins.

steps: Set the Smith bar so it rests at about mid-shin height.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the bar over your midfoot.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees, keeping your back straight and chest up, and grip the bar with an overhand grip just outside your legs.
Rotate the bar to unhook it, then stand up by extending your hips and knees, keeping the bar close to your body.
Stand up straight, fully extending your hips and knees.
Lower the bar back to mid-shin by hinging at the hips and bending your knees, keeping your back straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0752.note: Set a low (mid-shin) start position instead of hip height.

steps: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and step under it, resting it across your upper traps.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart, about a foot in front of the bar, so you lean back into it.
Unhook the bar by rotating it.
Bend your knees and let them travel forward as you lower your body, keeping your torso upright against the bar.
Continue descending until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your feet to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0755.note: Placed the feet forward of the bar with no step-back; primary glutes -> quadriceps.

steps: Set a bench parallel to the Smith machine and the bar at about hip height when you sit on the floor.
Sit on the floor with your upper back against the bench and the bar across your hip crease.
Place your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, and grip the bar on either side of your hips.
Unhook the bar, then push through your heels to drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0756.note: Loaded the Smith bar across the hips with the upper back on a bench; primary abdominals -> glutes.

steps: Set an incline bench under the Smith machine so the bar lowers to your upper chest.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar by rotating it and lower it slowly towards your upper chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment when the bar is just above your chest.
Push the bar back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0758.note: Changed to an underhand grip and set it up on an incline bench under the Smith bar.

steps: Set the Smith bar and safeties low enough that you can reach the bar with your feet when lying on the floor beneath it.
Lie on your back under the bar and place your feet on it, shoulder-width apart, with the bar over the middle of your feet.
Press the bar up slightly and rotate it to unhook it.
Bend your knees to lower the bar towards you until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Press the bar back up by extending your legs, without locking your knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0760.note: Replaced the plate-loaded leg press with lying under the Smith bar and pressing it with the feet.

steps: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and stand facing it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge forward at the hips with your back straight and grip the bar with an overhand grip, narrower than shoulder-width.
Unhook the bar by rotating it, letting it hang at arm's length.
Row the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0761.note: Replaced the seated handle row with a bent-over narrow-grip row on the Smith bar.

steps: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and stand facing it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor and grip the bar with a wide overhand grip.
Unhook the bar by rotating it, letting it hang at arm's length.
Row the bar to your upper chest with your elbows flared out to the sides, squeezing your rear delts.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0762.note: Replaced the chest-supported handle row with a wide-grip, elbows-out bent-over Smith row.

steps: Place a step under the Smith machine and set the bar just below shoulder height.
Step under the bar, rest it across your upper back, grip it overhand and unhook it by rotating it.
Stand with your heels on the edge of the step and the front of your feet hanging off, toes pointing forward.
Let the front of your feet drop below the step as far as is comfortable.
Raise your toes toward your shins as high as possible, keeping your legs straight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your toes back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0763.note: Made it a toe raise (dorsiflexion) on the heels; kept primary calves because tibialis isn't an allowed value, and removed hamstrings from secondary.

steps: Place a flat bench under the Smith machine so the bar sits directly above your lower chest when you lie down.
Lie on the bench with your feet flat on the floor and grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar by rotating it and hold it at arm's length.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Pause briefly, then press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0764.note: Replaced the standing overhand version with a flat-bench underhand Smith press. Revised again after the second review.

steps: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height, step under it and rest it across your upper traps with an overhand grip.
Unhook the bar by rotating it, with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back into a lunge position, keeping your back straight.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until your front thigh is about parallel to the ground.
Drive up through your front foot and bring your rear knee forward and up to hip height in a sprint position.
Step the same leg back into the lunge to begin the next repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0769.note: Replaced the rear-foot-elevated split squat with a back lunge that drives the rear knee up.

steps: Set the Smith bar at about mid-thigh height and stand with your back to it, feet shoulder-width apart.
Reach behind you and grasp the bar with your palms facing back, hands shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar by rotating it and hold it with straight arms behind your thighs.
Let your wrists drop so the bar lowers slightly.
Curl your wrists up, raising the bar behind you as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0771.note: Moved the bar behind the body, palms back, facing away from the machine.

yd-0778.note: Steps are correct; primary glutes -> chest (abdominals used since obliques isn't an allowed value). Revised again after the second review.
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor while bringing your right knee out to the side toward your right elbow.
At the bottom, your knee should be at or near your elbow, foot off the floor.
Push back up to the top while returning your right foot to the start.
Repeat with your left knee toward your left elbow.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Adjust the seat height and position on the stationary bike to ensure proper alignment.
Place your feet on the pedals and secure them with the straps if available.
Start pedaling at an easy, walking-like pace, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Maintain a steady rhythm and increase the resistance level if desired.
Continue pedaling for the desired duration, then gradually reduce your pace and resistance to cool down.
yd-0798.note: Equipment leverage machine -> machine ('stationary bike' isn't an allowed value); cut the post-workout stretch step to match the house style.

steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Engage your core and lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your body straight.
Push up explosively so your hands and feet leave the floor.
While in the air, briefly extend your arms straight out in front of you and your legs straight behind you.
Bring your hands back under your shoulders and land softly with your elbows bent, lowering straight into the next repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0803.note: Replaced the contradictory limb lift with the explosive airborne push-up with arms reaching forward.

steps: Attach a suspension trainer to a high anchor point and adjust the straps to about mid-length.
Stand facing away from the anchor point and hold the handles with your arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Lean forward onto the balls of your feet, keeping your body straight from head to heels and your core engaged.
Keeping your arms straight and hips extended, let your arms rise overhead as your body falls forward.
Lower as far as you can while keeping your body straight and maintaining tension in your abs.
Pull the handles back down in front of you with your abs and lats to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0805.note: Kept the body straight with the arms travelling overhead; left equipment as body weight because 'suspension trainer' isn't an allowed value.

yd-0812.note: Same movement as yd-0813 Triceps Dip (between Benches) once corrected.

steps: Place two benches parallel to each other, about leg-length apart.
Sit on one bench with your hands gripping the edge of the bench, fingers pointing forward.
Place your heels on the other bench with your legs straight and slide your butt off the bench, supporting your weight with your hands.
Bend your elbows and lower your body towards the ground between the benches, keeping your back close to the bench.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0813.note: Put the heels on a second bench so you dip between them (effectively the same movement as yd-0812).

steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat, placing your hands on the floor behind your hips with your fingers pointing forward.
Press through your hands to lift your hips off the floor and straighten your arms.
Slowly bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor without touching it, until your elbows are at about a 90-degree angle.
Press through your hands to straighten your elbows, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0815.note: Moved the dip to the floor with hands behind the hips instead of using a chair.

steps: Place your hands shoulder-width apart on a bar set at about waist height or on the edge of a bench, and walk your feet back so your body is straight and inclined.
Keep your arms straight and your body rigid from head to heels.
Bend your elbows, keeping them pointing forward, and lower your head below your hands.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then extend your elbows to push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0816.note: Added a support (bar or bench) and made it a bodyweight triceps extension.

steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself facing the cable machine.
Grasp the twin-handle attachment with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Sit down and position your thighs under the thigh pads, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up, maintaining a neutral spine.
Pull the handles down towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
Slowly release the handles and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0818.note: Changed the overhand grip to a neutral grip.

steps: Stand on a raised platform with the balls of your feet on the edge and your heels hanging off.
Bend forward at the hips to about 90 degrees and rest your hands on a stable support.
Place the load on your hips, using a partner, a weight belt or a donkey calf machine pad.
Lower your heels as far as possible to stretch your calves.
Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0833.note: Bent forward to 90 degrees and added load on the hips.

steps: Position yourself face down on a stability ball with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall for stability.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest or behind your head.
Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0835.note: Added the held weight to step 2.

steps: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward until your lower back is supported on the ball, with your feet flat on the ground and knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms overhead in line with your torso, letting your back extend over the ball.
Engage your abs and curl your torso up, keeping your arms fixed overhead.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your torso back over the ball to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0840.note: Changed sitting upright to lying with the lower back on the ball, crunching from extension.

steps: Attach weight using a dip belt or weighted vest, or hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Grab the pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0841.note: Added a first step that adds the load.

steps: Attach a weight plate to the end of the rope on a wrist roller, with the rope fully unwound.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the roller bar with both hands, palms facing down and arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Rotate the bar hand over hand, rolling your wrists to wind the rope around the bar and lift the weight.
Continue winding until the weight reaches the bar.
Slowly reverse the rotation to unwind the rope and lower the weight under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0859.note: Rewrote as winding the rope onto the roller bar hand over hand, then unwinding it.

yd-0860.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Set the cable pulley at the high position and attach a single handle.
Stand side-on to the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the handle with both hands above the shoulder nearest the machine, arms slightly bent.
Rotate your torso and pull the handle diagonally down and across your body to the outside of your opposite hip, pivoting your back foot.
Pause for a moment at the end of the rotation, then slowly return along the same path to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0862.note: Changed the horizontal twist to a high-to-low diagonal twist, standing side-on.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Raise your upper arms out to the sides to shoulder height, with your elbows bent 90 degrees, forearms parallel to the floor and palms facing down.
Keeping your upper arms still, rotate your forearms up until they are vertical, with the dumbbells above your elbows.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearms back to parallel.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0864.note: Added the 90-degree elbow bend with the upper arm abducted, rotating the forearms to vertical.

steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms by your sides.
Place your hands under your glutes for support.
Engage your core and lift your straight legs until they point toward the ceiling.
Curl your hips off the floor by pushing your feet straight up toward the ceiling.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower your hips and slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0865.note: Added the hip curl off the floor at the top of the leg raise.

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended, holding a dumbbell between your feet or wearing ankle weights.
Engage your core and lift your legs up in front of you, keeping them straight.
Continue lifting past parallel, curling your hips up and rolling your pelvis toward the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips and legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0866.note: Added the load and the pelvic curl past parallel.

steps: Anchor a band low behind your head, lie on your back with your legs straight, and hold the band with both hands with your arms extended overhead.
Engage your abs and lift your upper body and your right leg off the ground together, keeping the leg straight and your left leg on the floor.
Reach your hands toward your right foot against the pull of the band.
Slowly lower your upper body and leg back to the starting position.
Repeat with the left leg, alternating legs with each repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0969.note: Made it a true alternating V-up (one leg per rep) with the band anchored overhead for resistance.

steps: Loop a band from a high anchor in front of you around the ab wheel axle, then kneel on the floor holding the wheel handles with both hands.
Place the wheel on the ground in front of your knees with the band under tension.
Engage your core and slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body as far as you can while maintaining control, with the band helping support you.
Pause for a moment at the furthest point, then pull the wheel back toward your knees to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0971.note: Set up an ab wheel with a band assisting; removed 'place the band on the ground'.

steps: Lie flat on your back with your hands behind your head and a band looped around both feet.
Lift your feet off the ground with your knees bent so the band is taut.
Extend your left leg against the band while bringing your right knee towards your chest and twisting to bring your left elbow towards your right knee.
Extend your right leg against the band while bringing your left knee towards your chest and twisting to bring your right elbow towards your left knee.
Continue alternating sides in a pedaling motion, keeping your core engaged.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0972.note: Placed the band around both feet so each leg extends against it.

yd-0979.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at ankle height and loop the other end around your right ankle.
Stand facing the anchor point and step back to create tension in the band, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Hinge at the hips and lean forward, maintaining a neutral spine.
Drive your right leg straight back against the band, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0980.note: Looped the band around the working ankle and turned the user to face the anchor so the band resists the kick-back.

steps: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent to 90 degrees and a resistance band looped around your ankles.
Press your knees together and keep them in place.
Slowly rotate your feet outwards, away from each other, against the band.
Pause for a moment at the end of the rotation, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-0984.note: Reversed the motion: knees stay together and the feet move apart (internal rotation).

steps: Anchor the band high to one side of you and hold the free end in the hand nearest the anchor.
Raise your arm out to the side at shoulder height with your elbow straight and palm facing up.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, curl your hand toward your head, squeezing your biceps.
Pause for a moment, then slowly extend your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-0986.note: Moved the anchor high to the side with the upper arm at shoulder height so the curl works against the band.

steps: Stand in a split stance with your front foot on the middle of a resistance band and the top of your back foot resting on a bench behind you.
Hold the band in one hand at your shoulder.
Bend your front knee and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-0987.note: Rewrote as a rear-foot-elevated split squat with the band under the front foot, held in one hand.

yd-0992.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight, knees bent at 90 degrees, and feet flat on the ground.
Loop a resistance band around one ankle and anchor the other end at ankle height on the inside of that leg.
Keeping your knee still, rotate your shin and foot outward, away from your midline, against the band.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-0996.note: Changed to a band at the ankle with the foot rotating outward and the knee still (internal rotation).

steps: Stand on your left foot with the band looped under the ball of your foot and hold the ends taut at your shoulders.
Lift your right foot off the floor.
Slowly raise your left heel off the ground, lifting onto the ball of your foot against the band.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your left heel back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
yd-0999.note: Lifted the non-working foot and tensioned the band by holding the ends.

steps: Sit on a bench with your working heel on the floor and a band anchored low in front of you looped over the top of your forefoot.
Slide back until the band is under tension.
Keeping your heel on the ground, pull your toes up toward your shin against the band.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your toes back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
yd-1000.note: Rewrote as a band toe raise (dorsiflexion); kept calves as the closest allowed muscle and removed hamstrings and glutes.

yd-1003.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Wrap the band around a sturdy object at chest height.
Stand side-on to the anchor with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band at your chest with both hands.
Step away from the anchor to create tension in the band.
Engage your core and press the band straight up overhead, resisting the pull to rotate toward the anchor.
Hold for a moment, then slowly bring the band back to your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-1015.note: Changed the press direction from forward to overhead.

steps: Adjust the leverage machine to the appropriate height for your body.
Stand with the balls of your feet on the foot platform and your heels hanging off the edge.
Bend at the hips until your torso is about parallel to the floor, with the hip pad on your lower back and hips and your hands on the handles.
Lift your heels as high as possible, using the balls of your feet.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels below the platform.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1253.note: Added the bent-over donkey position under the hip pad.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Grasp the barbell with an underhand grip, about one and a half times shoulder width.
Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked in and your wrists straight.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest, then push it back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1258.note: Widened the reverse grip to clearly wide.

steps: Set a decline bench in front of a cable machine with the head end toward a low pulley.
Lie on the bench and grab the handle with one hand, bringing it to the side of your chest.
Press the handle up and slightly toward your hips until your arm is extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to your chest, letting your elbow travel down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1260.note: Fixed the setup and made it a press, not an elbow-only extension.

steps: Set a decline bench between two low pulleys.
Lie on the bench and grasp a handle in each hand, bringing them to the sides of your chest.
Press the handles up and slightly toward your hips until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your chest muscles.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1261.note: Positioned the bench between low pulleys so the press works against the cables.

steps: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley and set a decline bench beside the machine so the pulley is on your working side.
Lie down on the bench and grab the handle with your right hand.
Extend your arm straight up above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
With a controlled motion, lower your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Pause for a moment, then reverse the motion and bring your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left arm and repeat the exercise.
yd-1262.note: Moved the low pulley beside the bench on the working side.

steps: Place an exercise ball beside a low pulley and hold the handle in the hand nearest the machine.
Walk your feet forward until your head and upper back rest on the ball, then let your hips sink below shoulder level for an incline.
Extend your arm above your chest with a slight bend in your elbow and palm facing inward.
Slowly lower your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1264.note: Replaced the bench-plus-ball setup with a reclined incline on the ball beside a low pulley.

steps: Place an exercise ball in front of a low pulley, facing away from the machine, and hold the handle in one hand.
Walk your feet forward until your head and upper back rest on the ball, then let your hips sink below shoulder level for an incline.
Hold the handle at the side of your chest with your elbow bent.
Press the handle up and forward, extending your arm fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-1266.note: Replaced the bench-plus-ball setup with a reclined incline on the ball, low pulley behind.

steps: Attach the handles to the cables at the lowest pulley setting.
Stand in the center of the cable machine with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Grasp the handles with your palms facing forward and your arms down and out to the sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core.
Sweep your hands up and together in front of your upper chest.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Slowly lower the cables back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1270.note: Set the pulleys low with an upward sweep to upper-chest height.

steps: Kneel beside a stability ball.
Place your forearm and hand on top of the ball, out to the side at shoulder height.
Lean your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Hold the stretch for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-1272.note: Rewrote as a kneeling one-arm chest stretch with the forearm on the ball.

steps: Place two dumbbells slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and start in a high plank with your hands on the dumbbell handles.
Lower your chest below the level of your hands by bending your elbows.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1274.note: Put the hands on dumbbells and lowered the chest below hand level for extra range.

steps: Start in a high plank with each hand on a low platform, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift your hands off the platforms and drop them to the floor between them.
Land softly, absorbing the landing by lowering your chest into a push-up.
Push explosively so your hands leave the floor and land back on the platforms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1275.note: Rewrote as the plyometric drop from raised platforms.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball, then let your hips sink below shoulder level so your torso is on an incline.
Hold the dumbbells with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1278.note: Removed the incline bench; the incline comes from lowering the hips on the ball.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball, then let your hips sink below shoulder level so your torso is on an incline.
Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest, palm facing inwards.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Engage your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1280.note: Added the incline by dropping the hips below shoulder level.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand, feet flat on the ground.
Walk your feet forward and roll down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball, then let your hips sink below shoulder level so your torso is on an incline.
Hold the dumbbell at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-1282.note: Added the incline by dropping the hips below shoulder level.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Walk your feet forward and roll down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball, then let your hips sink below shoulder level so your torso is on an incline.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Press the dumbbells upward, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1283.note: Added the incline by dropping the hips below shoulder level.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet flat on the ground.
Walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball with your hips bridged level with your knees.
Extend your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inward.
Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause for a moment when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Engage your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1286.note: Fixed step 2 so the head, neck and upper back are supported with hips bridged.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet flat on the ground.
Walk your feet forward until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball with your hips bridged level with your knees.
Hold the dumbbell at the side of your chest with your elbow bent.
Press the dumbbell straight up over your chest until your arm is fully extended, keeping your core engaged and hips level.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-1290.note: Changed from a seated overhead press to a bridged chest press on the ball.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball with your hips bridged level with your knees.
Extend your arm straight up above your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arm straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1291.note: Added the bridged position on the ball.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand.
Walk your feet forward until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball with your hips bridged level with your knees.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you, keeping your hips level.
Hold the dumbbells above your chest with your palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1292.note: Changed from seated upright to a bridge on the ball with one leg extended.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and dumbbells in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball and your hips are level with your knees.
Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1293.note: Fixed step 2 so the upper back and head are on the ball with hips bridged.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and the dumbbell resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball down your back until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head while letting your hips sink toward the floor.
Raise the dumbbell back over your chest while driving your hips up into a bridge, squeezing your glutes.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1294.note: Combined the pullover with hips sinking and the bridge as the dumbbell returns.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball holding a dumbbell with both hands.
Walk your feet forward until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball with your hips bridged level with your knees.
Hold the dumbbell above your chest with your arms extended.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arms straight.
Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1295.note: Added the bridged position on the ball.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Bring your palms together in front of your chest with your elbows bent and out to the sides.
Press your palms together as hard as you can, squeezing your chest muscles.
Hold this position for a few seconds.
Release the squeeze and relax.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1297.note: Pressed the palms together in front of the chest so there is something to squeeze against.

steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grasp the handles with a narrow neutral grip, hands close together, and your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, squeezing the handles together as you press, exhaling during the movement.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1301.note: Narrowed the grip and added squeezing the handles together.

steps: Place a medicine ball on the floor in front of you and set up in a 3 point stance with both hands on the ball.
Explode forward and up, bringing the ball to your chest as you rise.
Chest-pass the ball out with both hands as hard as you can, following through.
Retrieve the ball and reset in the 3 point stance.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1303.note: Rewrote as an explosive chest pass from a crouched 3 point stance.

steps: Stand facing a wall about 1-2 meters away with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at chest level.
Explosively chest-pass the ball into the wall.
Catch the ball as it rebounds, bringing it back to your chest.
Immediately throw it again with minimal pause between catch and throw.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1304.note: Made it rapid repeated throws and catches against a wall.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the medicine ball at chest level.
Dip slightly and load the ball at your chest.
Explosively chest-pass the ball forward as far as you can, releasing it and following through.
Retrieve the ball and reset fully before the next throw.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1305.note: Made it a single maximal released chest pass with a full reset.

steps: Adjust the bench to a comfortable position on the smith machine.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, about one and a half times shoulder width.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows out to the sides.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1308.note: Widened the grip to about 1.5x shoulder width.

steps: Adjust the decline bench to the desired angle.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, about one and a half times shoulder width.
Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows pointed outwards.
Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1309.note: Widened the grip to about 1.5x shoulder width.

steps: Put on a weighted vest and start in a high plank with each hand on a low platform, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift your hands off the platforms and drop them to the floor between them.
Land softly, absorbing the landing by lowering your chest into a push-up.
Push explosively so your hands leave the floor and land back on the platforms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1310.note: Added the weighted vest and replaced the wide/narrow hand hops with the drop push-up from platforms.

steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to toe.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, letting them track out over your hands.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1311.note: Let the elbows track out instead of staying close to the sides.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at chest level.
Dip slightly, then step forward and explosively chest-pass the ball forward, releasing it.
Sprint after the ball straight out of the release.
Retrieve the ball, return to the start, and reset.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1312.note: Removed the roll/catch contradiction; it is now a chest pass followed by a sprint out of the release.

steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself facing the machine with your chest against the pad.
Grasp one handle with an overhand grip and keep your back straight.
Pull the handle towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blade back.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly extend your arm back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1313.note: Made it a one-arm row with a switch.

yd-1314.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench facing the backrest with your chest against it.
Grab the barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing forward) and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Adjust the cable machine so that the pulldown bar is at a height above your head.
Sit down on the seat and grab the pulldown bar with a wide overhand grip.
Sit upright and tilt your head slightly forward.
Pull the bar down behind your head to the base of your neck, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the bar back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1325.note: Changed the pull from the upper chest to behind the neck.

steps: Grab the pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands a few inches apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1327.note: Narrowed the grip to a few inches apart.

steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your feet.
Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Row the dumbbells up with your elbows flared out to the sides until your upper arms are level with your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your rear delts, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1328.note: Changed to an overhand grip with elbows flared to shoulder level; primary set to shoulders (rear delts).

steps: Set up an incline bench at a 30 to 45-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with an underhand grip and lie chest down on the bench with your feet on the floor.
Let your arm hang straight down with your palm facing forward.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your lower ribs, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1330.note: Changed to an underhand grip, lying chest down on the incline bench.

steps: Kneel on the floor in front of a stability ball.
Drape your torso over the ball and wrap your arms around it.
Let your back round over the ball and relax your head and neck.
Hold the stretch for the desired time, then slowly return to kneeling.
yd-1338.note: Rewrote as a kneeling hug over the ball with the back rounded.

steps: Kneel on the floor behind a stability ball.
Lean forward and drape your torso face down over the ball.
Let your arms and head hang down and your back round over the ball into a pyramid shape.
Hold the stretch for the desired time, then slowly return to kneeling.
yd-1341.note: Rewrote as the face-down pyramid over the ball; primary changed from lats to lower back.

steps: Kneel beside a stability ball and lie sideways over it with the ball under your ribs and hip.
Extend your legs and stagger your feet on the floor for balance.
Reach your top arm overhead, letting your side lengthen over the ball.
Hold the stretch for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-1342.note: Moved the ball under the ribs and hip so the side bends over it.

steps: Lie face down with your hips on the stability ball, hands on the floor in front of the ball, and toes on the floor.
Engage your core.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them until they are in line with your torso, using your lower back and glutes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1343.note: Put the hips on the ball instead of the toes.

steps: Adjust the seat height and sit on the machine with your thighs secured under the pad.
Grasp the handle with one hand using an overhand grip and fully extend your arm overhead.
Pull the handle down in a wide arc toward the same-side shoulder, driving your elbow toward your hip.
Squeeze your lat at the bottom, then slowly return the handle to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-1347.note: Changed the path to a wide arc to the same side and fixed the seated setup.

steps: Adjust the seat height and footplate position on the leverage machine.
Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the footplate.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Sit tall on the ground with your legs extended slightly wider than hip-width apart and your feet flexed.
Reach your arms forward at shoulder height.
Starting from your head, round your spine forward one vertebra at a time, reaching toward your feet.
Hold the stretch for a moment, then restack your spine one vertebra at a time to sit tall.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1363.note: Rewrote as the Pilates seated forward spine stretch.

steps: Set a barbell across your upper back and stand with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Keep your knees straight and your torso upright.
Raise your heels as high as possible, using your calves to lift your body.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1370.note: Moved the barbell to the upper back; kept the feet on the floor (no block, since it is a floor calf raise).

steps: Stand on top of a box or platform with your feet hip-width apart.
Step off the box and drop down.
Land softly on one foot with your knee and hip bent.
Hold the single-leg landing for 2-3 seconds, keeping your balance.
Step back up onto the box.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating landing legs.
yd-1374.note: Rewrote as a drop off the box to a single-leg stabilized landing.

steps: Stand facing a cable machine with the balls of your feet on a step and your heels hanging off.
Hold a handle attached to a low pulley in each hand at your sides.
Raise your heels off the ground by extending your ankles as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels below the step.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1375.note: Replaced the ankle strap with low-pulley handles for load; added a step for range.

steps: Stand facing a cable machine with the ball of one foot on a step and your heel hanging off.
Hold a low-pulley handle in the hand on the working side and hold the machine with the other hand for balance.
Lift your other foot off the ground.
Slowly raise your heel, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel below the step.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1376.note: Added the low-pulley handle for load and a step for range.

steps: Sit on the floor with your right leg extended in front of you.
Loop the middle of the rope around the ball of your right foot and hold an end in each hand.
Keeping your knee straight, pull the rope to draw your toes toward you until you feel a stretch in your calf.
Hold for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-1378.note: Rewrote as a seated rope calf stretch so the rope does the work.

steps: Stand on one foot with the ball of the foot on a step and your heel hanging off the edge.
Bend forward at the hips until your torso is about parallel to the floor, with your hands on a stable support.
Lift your other leg off the step.
Raise your heel as high as possible, using your calf muscles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel below the step.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1386.note: Added the bent-over donkey position and a step.

steps: Sit in the leg press machine and place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the sled, heels hanging off.
Extend your knees and release the safety handles.
Keeping your knees straight and fixed, push the sled away by pointing your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels to stretch your calves.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1391.note: Kept the knees fixed so the movement is only at the ankles.

steps: Sit on the leg press machine with your back against the backrest.
Place the ball of one foot on the lower edge of the sled with your heel hanging off, and rest the other foot on the floor or the frame.
Press the sled up and release the safety catches, keeping your working knee straight with a slight bend.
Let your heel drop toward you by flexing your ankle until you feel a stretch in your calf.
Push the sled away by extending your ankle as far as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the sled back to the stretched position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1392.note: Made it single-leg: one foot on the sled, other foot off, switch legs.

steps: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height, step under it and rest it across your upper back, gripping it with an overhand grip.
Unhook the bar and stand on one foot flat on the floor, lifting the other foot behind your working ankle.
Raise your heel as high as possible by extending your ankle, keeping your knee straight.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower your heel back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1393.note: Replaced the impossible under-the-bar setup with a standing single-leg calf raise from the floor, bar on the upper back.

steps: Place a bench under the Smith machine with a block or weight plate in front of it, and sit on the bench.
Place the ball of one foot on the block with your heel hanging off, and rest the other foot on the floor.
Lower the bar onto your working thigh just above the knee, using a pad if needed, and unhook it while holding it with your hands.
Lower your heel as far as possible to stretch your calf.
Raise your heel as high as possible by extending your ankle.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1395.note: Added the Smith setup: seated on a bench, ball of one foot on a block, bar resting across the working knee.

steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, and place your hands on the floor behind your hips with your fingers pointing forward.
Press through your hands to lift your hips off the floor.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your hips nearly touch the floor.
Push yourself back up by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1399.note: Moved the dip onto the floor with hands behind the hips instead of on a bench edge.

steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart and arms fully extended.
Pull yourself up explosively, driving the bar toward your lower chest.
As the bar reaches your chest, lean your shoulders forward over the bar and quickly rotate your wrists and elbows over it.
Press down on the bar to straighten your arms into a support position above the bar.
Reverse the transition under control and lower yourself back to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1401.note: Added the transition over the bar and the press to straight-arm support; it was only a pull-up before.

steps: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp a handle attached to the low pulley with an overhand grip, palm facing down.
Keep your elbow close to your side and slowly curl your forearm up towards your shoulder.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1413.note: Fixed the grip to overhand, palm down, and added switching arms.

steps: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the pad and your arm extended over the edge of the bench, holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip, palm facing down.
Lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is fully extended.
Curl the dumbbell back up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary and your palm facing down.
Squeeze at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1414.note: Changed the grip to overhand (palm down) for the reverse curl.

steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing in and your thumb up.
Rest your forearm on your thigh with your wrist just past your knee, letting the front of the dumbbell dip toward the floor.
Keeping your forearm stationary, lift the front of the dumbbell by bending your wrist upward toward your thumb.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other hand.
yd-1415.note: Changed to a neutral (thumb-up) grip with the wrist bending toward the thumb.

steps: Lie on your back with your heels on top of the stability ball and your arms by your sides, palms down.
Lift your hips off the ground to form a straight line from your shoulders to your heels.
Lift one leg off the ball, keeping the other heel on the ball.
Roll the ball toward your glutes by bending the supporting knee while kicking the free leg diagonally up and across your body.
Straighten the supporting leg to roll the ball back out while you return the free leg, keeping your hips lifted.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1417.note: Added the hamstring curl on the supporting leg during the diagonal kick; primary changed to hamstrings.

steps: Lie on your back with your legs extended.
Bend both knees and draw them toward your chest.
Wrap your arms around your shins and gently pull your knees closer until you feel a stretch in your glutes and lower back.
Hold for a moment, then release and extend your legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1418.note: Rewrote it as the supine knees-to-chest hug; secondary changed to lower back and hamstrings because quads aren't involved. The name has a typo ('Keens'). Name typo: Keens. After the rename it is the same movement as Hug_Knees_To_Chest, so the build drops it.
yd-1418.name: Hug Knees to Chest

steps: Start in a modified push-up position with your knees on the floor, hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line from head to knees.
Bend your elbows to lower your forearms to the floor one at a time, so you rest on your forearms with elbows under your shoulders.
Pause for a moment, then press through your palms to straighten your elbows and lift your forearms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1421.note: Primary changed to triceps as flagged; also added the knees-down 'modified' setup and tidied the hands-to-forearms transition.

steps: Adjust the machine to your desired assistance level.
Stand on the foot platform and grip the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing you, about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your chest up and shoulders back, engage your core, and slightly bend your knees.
Pull your body up by flexing your elbows and driving your elbows down towards your sides.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1431.note: Changed the grip to underhand at shoulder width. Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Set the Smith machine bar at upper-chest height and step under it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders against your collarbone and take a clean grip with your fingertips under the bar just outside your shoulders.
Drive your elbows high and forward, then stand up and rotate the bar to unhook it.
Keeping your torso upright and elbows high, squat down by bending your knees and hips, letting your knees travel forward.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1433.note: Added the clean-grip front rack (fingertips under the bar, elbows high) and an upright squat in place of the sit-back cue.

steps: Set the Smith machine bar at about mid-chest height and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Step under the bar and set it low on your rear delts, just below the spine of your shoulder blades rather than on your traps.
Grip the bar with your elbows pulled back to hold it in place.
Stand up to lift the bar, rotate it to unhook it, and brace your core.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, letting your torso lean further forward than in a high-bar squat.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Drive through your feet to stand back up, extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1434.note: Moved the bar onto the rear delts, added the forward lean, and changed unracking to unhooking the Smith bar. Cut from 11 steps to 8.

steps: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about mid-chest height and step under it.
Place the bar low on your rear delts, just below the spine of your shoulder blades, and grip it with your elbows pulled back.
Lift the bar off the rack, step back, and set your feet shoulder-width apart with your toes slightly turned out.
Brace your core, push your hips back and bend your knees, letting your torso lean forward more than in a high-bar squat.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Pause for a moment, then drive up through your feet to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1435.note: Specified low-bar placement on the rear delts and a hip-dominant, forward-leaning squat.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the barbell overhand with a wide grip, about one and a half times shoulder width.
Lift the barbell to shoulder height, keeping your forearms close to vertical.
Press the barbell overhead, extending your arms fully.
Lower the barbell back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1457.note: Made the grip clearly wide with near-vertical forearms, and split out the final repeat step.

steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Sit upright with your arms at your sides and let the bar rest on your thighs.
Keeping your elbows by your sides, exhale and curl the ez barbell upwards towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the ez barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1458.note: Replaced the unworkable upper-arms-on-thighs position with upright sitting, elbows at the sides, and the bar starting on the thighs.

steps: Start in a forearm plank with your elbows directly below your shoulders, palms flat on the floor, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Press your palms into the floor to straighten your elbows, lifting your forearms off the ground until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly bend your elbows to lower your forearms back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1467.note: Rewrote it as a triceps extension push-up: press from the forearms up to straight arms and lower back down.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hold onto a stable object with one hand for balance.
Rise onto the balls of your feet.
Push your knees forward and lower your body while leaning your torso back, keeping your hips extended so your body stays in a straight line from knees to head.
Continue lowering until your knees are well forward and you feel a deep stretch in your quads, or as far as you can control.
Pause for a moment, then straighten your knees to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1489.note: Added the defining mechanics: up on the toes, knees forward, hips extended with a backward lean. Removed 'push through heels' and 'torso upright'.

steps: Stand facing a large tire about an arm's length away with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the sledge hammer with one hand near the end of the handle and the other near the head.
Swing the hammer up and back over one shoulder, keeping your top hand near the head.
Bring the hammer down onto the tire, sliding your top hand down the handle to meet your bottom hand and bending your hips and knees as you strike.
Control the rebound and switch your hand positions to swing over the other shoulder on the next strike.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating sides.
yd-1496.note: Added the backswing, hand slide, tire target and alternating sides. Changed equipment 'hammer' (not an allowed value) to 'other'.

steps: Stand in front of the stability ball, facing away from it.
Place the top of your left foot on the ball behind you and step your right foot forward into a lunge stance, front knee over your ankle.
Lower your hips and press them forward, tucking your pelvis slightly, until you feel a stretch in the front of your left hip.
Hold for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-1559.note: Put the rear foot on the ball so the stretch lands in the rear hip flexor. Primary changed to quadriceps; 'hip flexors' isn't an allowed value.

steps: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend one leg forward with your heel on the floor, toes pointing up and knee straight.
Place your hands on your bent leg's thigh and keep your back flat.
Hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch in the hamstring of your straight leg.
Hold for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-1560.note: Replaced the incoherent bridge sequence with a seated single-leg hip hinge stretch.

steps: Stand upright and loop a strap around the ball of one foot, holding the ends with both hands.
Step that foot forward a short distance and rest it on its heel with your toes pointing up, keeping the leg straight.
Pull the strap toward you to draw your toes back.
Keeping your back flat, hinge forward from your hips with a slight bend in your back knee until you feel a stretch in your hamstring and calf.
Hold for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-1599.note: Placed the strapped foot forward on its heel and added pulling the strap. Merged the end into one hold-and-switch step.

steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the leverage machine.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Rest your upper arms on the preacher pad, ensuring your elbows are fully extended.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the handles towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1616.note: Changed the grip to overhand, palms down.

steps: Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured, holding a dumbbell in one hand at the side of your chest with your palm facing in.
Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is extended, keeping your palm facing in.
Lower the dumbbell back to the side of your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Press the dumbbell back up to the extended position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1617.note: Specified the neutral (palm-in) grip and cleaned up the start and lowering positions.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Lower your hips toward the floor so your torso is inclined, with your shoulders higher than your hips.
Hold the dumbbells beside your chest with your palms facing each other and your elbows tucked toward your sides.
Press the dumbbells up, keeping your palms facing each other, until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1618.note: Added lowering the hips to create the incline, and tucked the elbows to match a neutral-grip press.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Lower your hips toward the floor so your torso is inclined, with your shoulders higher than your hips.
Hold the dumbbell beside your chest with your palm facing inward and your elbow close to your body.
Press the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, straightening your arm.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1620.note: Added lowering the hips to create the incline.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball, with your hips lifted in line with your knees.
Hold the dumbbell beside your chest with your palm facing in and your elbow close to your body.
Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is fully extended, keeping your palm facing in.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1621.note: Changed it from a seated overhead press to a neutral-grip chest press in a bridge on the ball.

steps: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the ground, holding a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, palm facing your head.
Press the dumbbell up over your lower chest until your arm is extended.
Lower the dumbbell to your lower chest, keeping your elbow tucked close to your body.
Press the dumbbell back up until your arm is fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-1622.note: Changed it from a seated overhead press to a lying underhand-grip chest press.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing toward your head.
Extend your arms straight up towards the ceiling, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells towards your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1624.note: Changed to an underhand grip, palms toward the head, with elbows tucked and the dumbbells lowered to the lower chest.

steps: Set a decline bench under the Smith machine.
Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar and lower it slowly towards your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the bar back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1626.note: Specified an underhand close grip and clarified the decline bench setup.

steps: Sit on a preacher curl bench and grip the inner (close) handles of the ez barbell with an underhand grip, hands narrower than shoulder width.
Rest your triceps on the pad and fully extend your arms, keeping your back straight.
Slowly curl the barbell towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1627.note: Specified the close grip on the inner handles.

steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands a few inches apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Exhale and curl the bar up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1630.note: Narrowed the grip to hands a few inches apart.

steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended and the bar in front of your thighs.
Drive your elbows back as you curl the bar up, keeping it in contact with or close to your torso.
Continue dragging the bar up your torso until it reaches your lower chest.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the bar along the same path back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1632.note: Added the drag: elbows go back while the bar slides up the torso.

steps: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulley is at the lowest position.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the cable handle with an overhand grip, palm facing down, and position your upper arm against the preacher bench pad.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Slowly curl your forearm towards your upper arm, keeping your upper arm stationary against the pad.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1635.note: Changed the grip to overhand and merged the switch-arms step to stay within 8 steps.

steps: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and sit or kneel facing the machine, such as at a lat pulldown station.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, with your arms extended up and forward toward the pulley.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the bar down toward your forehead by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly straighten your elbows to return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1638.note: Kept the high pulley ('pulldown') but changed it to a high-cable biceps curl toward the forehead; the old version was a triceps pushdown.

steps: Attach a rope handle to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp one end of the rope with a neutral grip, palm facing in.
Position your upper arm against the preacher bench pad with your arm extended.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Slowly curl the rope towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary and your palm facing in.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the rope back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
Attach a straight bar or handle to a high pulley and sit on a bench facing the machine.
Grasp the attachment with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and extend your arms up and forward toward the pulley so your upper arms are at about head height.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the attachment toward your head.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly straighten your elbows back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1643.note: Raised the upper arms toward a high pulley and curled toward the head, instead of keeping the elbows at the sides.

steps: Attach a cable handle to the lowest setting on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the cable handle with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and arms fully extended.
Lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and your heels down.
Staying in the squat, curl the cable handle towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Pause for a moment at the top of the curl, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1644.note: Swapped 'knees behind your toes' for 'heels down' and said to stay in the squat while curling.

steps: Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, upper arms on the pad, palms facing each other and arms fully extended.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, curl one dumbbell up with your thumb pointing up.
Continue raising it until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, then curl with the other arm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating arms.
yd-1646.note: Made it alternating, one arm at a time, with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Lift one foot off the floor by bending the knee and balance on the other leg.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
yd-1653.note: Changed the stance to a true one-leg stork stance.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing forward.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips until your thighs are about parallel to the ground, keeping your chest up.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.
At the top, keep your elbows close to your sides and curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your biceps, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to your sides.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1655.note: Added the squat before each curl; added quadriceps and glutes to secondary.
