steps: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang down and out wide to the sides below bench level, palms facing up.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and wide, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1662.note: Added the wide arm position, with the arms hanging out to the sides below the bench.

steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand and raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, palms facing up.
Keeping your upper arms stationary at shoulder height, curl the dumbbells toward your head.
Pause for a moment, squeezing your biceps, then slowly straighten your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1664.note: Raised the upper arms to shoulder height and curled toward the head.

steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing forward.
Extend your arm fully, letting it hang straight down towards the floor.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1665.note: Changed to a supinated grip (palm forward).

steps: Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie chest-down on it with a dumbbell in one hand, arm hanging straight toward the floor with an overhand grip, palm facing down.
Keeping your upper arm vertical and stationary, curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder by flexing your elbow.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1667.note: Added the chest-down position on an incline bench with the arm hanging vertically.

steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm facing your torso.
Keep your elbow close to your torso and your upper arm stationary.
Exhale and curl the weight while contracting your biceps, keeping your palm facing in.
Continue to raise the weight until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1671.note: Made it one dumbbell in one hand, with switching arms.

steps: Sit on a preacher curl bench and hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip.
Rest your upper arm on the preacher bench pad, allowing your arm to fully extend.
Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary.
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrist so that your palm faces down.
Slowly lower the dumbbell with the overhand grip, then rotate your palm back up at the bottom.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1672.note: Fixed the Zottman rotation: palm down at the top, lower overhand, rotate back at the bottom.

steps: Kneel behind an exercise ball and drape the back of one upper arm over the top of it, holding a dumbbell with an underhand grip and your arm extended.
Steady the ball with your other hand.
Keeping your upper arm stationary on the ball, exhale and curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder.
Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1673.note: Changed it to kneeling behind the ball and using it as the preacher pad.

steps: Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie chest-down on it with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight toward the floor with an overhand grip.
Keeping your upper arms vertical and stationary, exhale and curl the weights toward your shoulders.
Continue to raise the dumbbells until your elbows are fully bent.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1675.note: Changed from a standing hammer curl to a chest-down incline curl with an overhand grip.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Lift one foot off the floor and hold that leg raised throughout the set.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm fully extended.
Place your other hand on your hip for stability.
Slowly curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your bicep.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and legs.
yd-1679.note: Added the raised leg; merged the switch step to stay within 8 steps.

steps: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet wider than shoulder-width and hold an ez barbell with a close underhand grip on the inner handles.
Lean forward and brace the backs of both upper arms against your inner thighs, arms extended.
Curl the barbell up towards your shoulders while keeping your upper arms stationary against your thighs.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1682.note: Added the close grip and braced both upper arms on the inner thighs.

steps: Set a sturdy bar at about waist height and start in a push-up position on the floor beside it, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and body in a straight line.
Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Move under the bar and grip it with an overhand grip, arms extended, heels on the floor and body straight.
Pull your chest up to the bar by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating one push-up and one row.
yd-1689.note: Paired the push-up with an inverted row for a real pull, and added middle back and biceps to secondary. The name is vague; this is my best guess.

steps: Start in a high plank position with both hands close together on top of the medicine ball under your chest.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Push back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1701.note: Put both hands together on top of the ball.

steps: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked, bottom knee slightly bent for stability and your head resting on your arm.
Have a partner kneel behind you and support your top leg at the knee and ankle.
Keeping your top leg straight with your toes facing forward, have your partner slowly raise it up and away from your bottom leg until you feel a stretch in your inner thigh.
Keep your hips stacked while your partner holds the leg in place.
Hold for the desired time, then have your partner lower your leg and switch sides.
yd-1712.note: Changed to a partner raising the top leg (abduction) so the stretch lands in the adductors.

steps: Lie face down on the ground with your legs straight.
Have a partner kneel beside you, bend your right knee, and hold your ankle.
Have your partner gently push your heel toward your glutes while your hips stay pressed into the floor, until you feel a stretch in the front of your thigh.
Hold for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-1714.note: Primary changed to quadriceps; 'hip flexors' isn't allowed, so secondary is empty. Also made it partner-assisted to match the name.

steps: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Clasp your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
Have a partner stand behind you and hold your elbows.
Have your partner gently draw your elbows back while you keep your chest up, until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Hold for the desired time, then slowly release.
yd-1716.note: Changed to a partner drawing the elbows back while seated on the ball; dropped triceps from secondary.

steps: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Hold the barbell with a close overhand grip and press it overhead to lockout, upper arms close to your head.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, lower the barbell behind your neck by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1718.note: Start from an overhead lockout and lower behind the neck.

steps: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handle with one hand using an overhand grip.
Pin your elbow to your side with your elbow bent to about 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and push the handle down until your arm is fully extended.
Pause for a moment, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1723.note: Single handle on a high pulley, elbow pinned at 90 degrees, push to full extension.

steps: Attach a rope to a low pulley and set an incline bench with its back facing the machine.
Grasp the rope with an overhand grip and lie back on the bench with your head toward the machine.
Extend your arms overhead with your upper arms close to your head.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1725.note: Now performed lying on the incline bench; moved the rope to a low pulley so it pulls from behind the head.

steps: Set two pulleys to the lowest position and stand facing the machine between them, holding a handle in each hand with the cables crossed and palms facing in.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent.
Raise your upper arms alongside your torso, parallel to the floor, with your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, extend your elbows to push the handles back until your arms are straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1728.note: Added the low pulley setup, the forward hinge, and upper arms parallel to the floor.

steps: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight, until your torso is close to your thighs.
Raise your upper arms alongside your torso with your elbows bent at 90 degrees and forearms hanging toward the floor.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, extend one elbow to push the dumbbell back until your arm is fully straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your elbow back to 90 degrees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating arms.
yd-1730.note: Pinned the upper arm alongside the torso at 90 degrees so the work happens at the elbow only.

steps: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Lie back and press the dumbbells up over your head with your palms facing each other.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, lower the dumbbells beside your head by bending only your elbows.
Pause for a moment, then extend your elbows back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1733.note: Changed from an incline press to a triceps extension that hinges only at the elbows.

steps: Lie face down over the exercise ball with your torso supported and your feet on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards.
Raise your upper arms alongside your torso, parallel to the floor, with your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Extend your elbows to push the dumbbells back until your arms are straight, squeezing your triceps.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1734.note: Changed it to lying face down over the ball, with upper arms parallel to the floor.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground, your back straight, and a dumbbell in one hand.
Press the dumbbell overhead so your upper arm is vertical beside your head, palm facing in.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow.
Extend your elbow to raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1736.note: Start from an overhead lockout with the upper arm vertical and lower the dumbbell behind the head.

steps: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight, until your torso is close to your thighs.
Raise your upper arms alongside your torso with your elbows by your sides and bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, extend your elbows to push the dumbbells back until your arms are straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1737.note: Pinned the upper arms alongside the torso and started from 90 degrees; removed the contradictory 'elbows close to your head' cue.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Pin your upper arms beside your torso, parallel to the floor, with your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arm still, extend one arm straight back at the elbow until it is fully straight.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend the elbow to return the dumbbell to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1739.note: Fixed upper arms at 90-degree elbows and made the extension one arm at a time to match 'alternating'.

steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in your right hand, then lift your right foot off the floor so you balance on your left leg.
Bend your standing knee slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Bring your right upper arm up beside your torso, parallel to the floor, with your elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keeping your upper arm still, extend your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bend your elbow to return the dumbbell to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-1742.note: Added the stork stance (balance on the leg opposite the working arm) and a fixed upper arm.

steps: Sit on the stability ball and place your hands on the ball just behind your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Walk your feet forward and slide your hips off the front of the ball, supporting your weight on your hands with your arms straight and knees bent.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them pointing back, until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Push through your hands to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1744.note: Rewrote as a real dip: hips moved off the front of the ball and lowered by bending the elbows.

steps: Sit on an exercise ball holding a dumbbell, then walk your feet forward until your head, neck and upper back rest on the ball.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders, with your feet flat on the floor.
Hold the dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest.
Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Pause for a moment, then extend your elbows to raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1746.note: Changed from a seated overhead extension to the supine version with the upper back on the ball and hips bridged.

steps: Place a flat bench inside a power rack and set the safety pins so the bar sits a few inches above your chest when you lie down.
Rest the barbell on the pins and lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Press the barbell from a dead stop on the pins up to full lockout.
Lower the barbell under control until it rests back on the pins, letting it settle for a moment.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1751.note: Rewrote as a bench press from a dead stop on safety pins set above the chest.

steps: Place two benches parallel to each other, about shoulder-width apart, with a third bench in front of them.
Sit between the two parallel benches, place a hand on each bench beside your hips, and rest your heels on the third bench with your legs straight.
Straighten your arms to lift your hips so your weight is supported by your hands and heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your body until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1753.note: Added the three-bench setup: hands on two parallel benches, heels on a third.

steps: Place two benches parallel to each other, about shoulder-width apart, with a third bench in front of them.
Sit between the parallel benches with a hand on each bench beside your hips and rest your heels on the third bench with your legs straight.
Have a weight plate placed on your lap, then straighten your arms to lift your hips.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping your back close to the benches, until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1754.note: Added the three-bench setup (feet elevated) and a plate on the lap.

steps: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands gripping the edge next to your hips.
Slide your butt off the front of the bench with your legs extended in front of you, and have a weight plate placed on your lap.
Keep your back close to the bench and your elbows slightly bent.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1755.note: Added a plate on the lap; the rest of the bench dip was already right.

yd-1758.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Stand on your left leg with your arms extended in front of you.
Lift your right foot off the ground and extend the leg straight out in front of you.
Slowly lower your body by bending your left knee and pushing your hips back, keeping your right leg straight and off the floor.
Keep your chest up and your left heel down as you lower yourself.
Descend until your hamstring rests on your calf at the bottom of the squat.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your left foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-1759.note: Changed to full depth with the free leg held straight off the floor; primary set to quadriceps (the main mover in a pistol).

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.
Engage your core and lift your legs by flexing your hips and knees until your thighs are parallel to the ground.
Continue the movement by curling your pelvis up and bringing your knees toward your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips and legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1764.note: Added the pelvic curl past parallel that sets this apart from a hanging knee raise.

steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt around your waist, or hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Position yourself between the high parallel bars with your hands gripping the bars and your arms fully extended.
Bend your elbows and lower your body until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1767.note: Added the dip belt or dumbbell for load.

steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and lean your torso forward slightly.
Hook your right hand under your right thigh just behind the knee, palm facing up, with your arm extended.
Keeping your upper arm still and your leg relaxed, curl your leg up toward your chest by bending your elbow.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the leg back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1770.note: Swapped the dumbbell for your own leg as the resistance, to match the body weight equipment.

steps: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and place your hands on the floor in front of you, shoulder-width apart, arms straight.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your head.
Bend only your elbows, lowering your body until your forearms rest on the floor.
Pause for a moment, then press through your palms to straighten your elbows and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1771.note: Replaced the close-grip push-up with a kneeling extension: lower to the forearms by bending only the elbows, then press back up.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and your elbows bent at your sides with your forearms pointing up.
Press your elbows into the floor to lift your chest and upper back off the ground, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top for a moment, squeezing your upper back muscles.
Slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-1772.note: Changed from prone palm pressing to supine, driving the elbows into the floor.

steps: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or door handle and hold both ends in one hand.
Stand facing the anchor with your feet close to it, then lean back until your arm is fully extended and your body is straight.
Pull your body toward the anchor by bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade back.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-1773.note: Anchored the towel and made it a one-arm bodyweight row toward the anchor.

steps: Lie on your side next to a bench and rest the inside of your top foot or knee on the bench.
Prop yourself up on your forearm, keeping your elbow directly below your shoulder, with your bottom leg on the floor.
Press your top leg down into the bench to lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your feet.
Lift your bottom leg up to meet the underside of the bench.
Slowly lower your bottom leg and hips back toward the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-1775.note: Replaced top-leg abduction with the Copenhagen adduction: top leg on a bench, bottom leg lifted.

steps: Start by lying face down on the floor.
Place your forearms on the ground, with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Extend your legs straight out behind you, with your toes on the ground.
Lift your body onto your forearms and toes, keeping a straight line from your head to your heels.
Have a partner place a weight plate on your upper back.
Hold this position for the desired amount of time.
Have the plate removed, then lower your body back down to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2135.note: Added a plate on the upper back.

steps: Adjust the seat height and handlebar position to a comfortable level.
Sit facing the ergometer with your back straight and your feet flat on the floor or footrest.
Grasp the handles with your hands and position your arms at a 90-degree angle.
Start pedaling with your hands, pushing and pulling the handles in a controlled motion.
Continue pedaling for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
yd-2139.note: Feet now go on the floor or footrest, not pedals; 'upper body ergometer' isn't an allowed equipment value, so set it to machine.

steps: Stand facing the SkiErg with your feet hip-width apart and take a handle in each hand.
Reach your arms overhead with a slight bend in your elbows.
Drive the handles down by pulling with your lats and pressing with your triceps, hinging at the hips and bending your knees slightly.
Finish with the handles past your hips and your torso leaning forward.
Let the handles rise as you return to standing tall with your arms overhead.
Continue for the desired time or distance.
yd-2142.note: Rewrote as a standing SkiErg stroke with a hip hinge; primary set to lats; 'skierg machine' isn't allowed, so set to machine.

steps: Sit on the roller with it under your right glute and place your hands on the floor behind you for support.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee, keeping your left foot flat on the floor.
Lean slightly toward your right side to put your weight on the right glute.
Slowly roll back and forth over the glute, pausing on any tight spots.
Continue for the desired time, then switch sides.
yd-2202.note: Replaced the contradictory setup with a figure-four glute roll on one side.

steps: Start in a forearm plank with your forearms on the floor and your shins resting on the roller.
Keep your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Push your body backward by reaching your arms forward from the shoulders, letting your legs roll on the roller while keeping your hips level.
Pull your body forward by bringing your elbows back under your shoulders.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2204.note: Changed from a rollout to a body saw: forearms on the floor, shins on the roller, rocking from the shoulders.

steps: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides, palms down.
Squeeze a roller between your knees and lift your legs so your thighs are vertical and your knees are bent at 90 degrees.
Engaging your abs, curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest while holding the roller in place.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2206.note: Picked one setup (roller squeezed between the knees, no rolling) and wrote a clean reverse crunch.

steps: Kneel on the floor and place a roller in front of you, slightly to your right.
Rest your right forearm on the roller with your thumb up, and place your left hand on the floor for support.
Sit your hips back toward your heels and roll the roller forward and out to the right, sinking your chest toward the floor.
Pause for a few seconds in the stretch along your right side, then roll the roller back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-2207.note: Rewrote as a kneeling one-sided lat stretch rolling forward and out to the side.

steps: Sit on the floor with the roller behind you, perpendicular to your body, and your knees bent with your feet flat.
Lie back so the roller is under your mid-back, with your hands behind your head.
Lift your hips slightly off the floor.
Push with your legs to roll your body so the roller moves from your mid-back up to your upper back.
Pause for a moment, then slowly roll back to your mid-back.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2208.note: Added the knees-bent, hips-lifted setup that drives the roll; muscles changed to match a mid/upper back roll (hamstrings/glutes were wrong).

steps: Sit on the floor with your left leg extended and your right knee bent, right foot flat on the floor.
Hold the roller with both hands, palms facing down, resting it on your thighs with your arms straight.
Sit up tall and engage your core.
Raise the roller up past shoulder level and overhead, keeping your arms straight.
At the top, pull your shoulder blades down and back without bending your arms.
Slowly lower the roller back down to your thighs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-2209.note: Added the single-leg position and the depress/retract phase from the name; primary set to shoulders, since it's a shoulder flexion/scapular drill, not a chest movement.

steps: Stand in a staggered stance with your left foot forward and your knees slightly bent.
Raise both hands to guard your face, with your right hand by your chin.
Rotate your hips and pivot on the ball of your left foot as you swing your left arm in a horizontal arc toward the target.
Keep your left elbow bent at about 90 degrees with your forearm parallel to the floor through the punch.
Return your left hand to the guard position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2271.note: Changed from a straight punch to a hook: staggered stance, bent-arm horizontal arc, pivot on the lead foot.

steps: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot point.
Sit with your back against the pad, place your elbows on the arm pads, and lightly hold the handles with your arms overhead.
Keep your core engaged and your back against the pad.
Drive your elbows down and forward in an arc until your upper arms reach your torso, squeezing your lats.
Pause for a moment, then slowly let your arms return overhead to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2285.note: Replaced the row-like pull with the pullover arc from overhead down to the torso.

steps: Adjust the hip machine so its pivot lines up with your hip and the pad sits behind your working thigh, just above the knee.
Stand on your other leg on the platform, facing the machine, and grip the handles for stability.
Engage your glutes and push the pad backward by extending your hip, keeping your torso upright.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly return your leg to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-2286.note: Replaced the impossible seated setup with a standing multi-hip extension.

steps: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad and adjust the seat so your legs are almost straight when your feet are on the platform.
Place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform, with your heels hanging off.
Grasp the handles or side supports for stability.
Press the platform away by pointing your toes and extending your ankles as far as possible.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly let your heels drop back toward you to stretch your calves, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2289.note: Fixed the setup and direction: press the platform away by pointing the toes, then let the heels drop under control.

yd-2292.note: Picture removed: it showed a different movement.

steps: Stand behind a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.
Rest your upper arms against the pad and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders while keeping your upper arms stationary.
At the top of the movement, rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing down.
Slowly lower the dumbbells with your palms facing down until your arms are extended.
At the bottom, rotate your wrists so your palms face up again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2293.note: The lowering is now fully palms down, rotating back only at the bottom (the Zottman eccentric).

steps: Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up and elbows resting on the pad.
Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms stationary and your palms facing up.
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing down.
Slowly lower the dumbbells with your palms facing down until your arms are extended.
At the bottom, rotate your wrists so your palms face up again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2294.note: The lowering is now fully palms down, rotating back only at the bottom.

steps: Sit on the stability ball, then walk your feet forward until your lower back rests on the ball, with your feet flat and knees bent at 90 degrees.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Let your upper back extend back over the ball until you feel a stretch in your abs.
Engaging your abs, curl your upper body up and forward as far as you can.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back over the ball.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2297.note: Changed from sitting upright to lying with the lower back on the ball, extending over it before each crunch.

steps: Set up a bar at waist height and lie underneath it.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees to about 90 degrees with your feet flat on the floor, keeping your body straight from knees to shoulders.
Pull your chest up towards the bar by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2300.note: Changed step 3 to the bent-knee, feet-flat position.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing forward.
Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Let your arms hang straight down, fully extended, with a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your lower ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2327.note: Changed the grip to underhand and the row target to the lower ribs.

steps: Attach a pair of ab straps (arm slings) to a pull-up bar and slide your upper arms into them so you hang by your elbows with your legs straight down.
Engage your core and lift your straight legs up in front of you until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2333.note: Added the arm slings; 'ab straps' isn't an allowed equipment value, so set it to other.

steps: Sit on the machine and adjust the pad so it rests on your lower thighs, just above your knees.
Place the balls of your feet on the platform, with your heels hanging off the edge.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the seat for stability.
Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting the pad by extending your ankles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels below the platform for a stretch.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2335.note: Pad now rests on the lower thighs and the heels lift the pad (seated calf raise direction).

steps: Attach a pair of ab straps (arm slings) to a pull-up bar and slide your upper arms into them so you hang by your elbows, with your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Engage your core and lift your knees towards your chest, bringing them as close to your elbows as possible.
Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2355.note: Added the arm slings; equipment set to other, since ab straps isn't an allowed value.

steps: Position yourself on wide-set or angled parallel bars with your hands wider than shoulder width, arms fully extended and body suspended in the air.
Lean your torso forward and lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest is just above the bars.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2363.note: Specified the wide hand position and the forward lean.

steps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands close together under your chest and your knees hip-width apart.
Lower your upper body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Pause for a moment when your chest is just above the ground.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2398.note: Changed step 1 to a close hand position.

steps: Set the thigh pads of a lat pulldown station low and kneel on the seat facing away from the machine, hooking your ankles under the pads.
Keep your body straight from your knees to your head, with your hands in front of your chest.
Slowly lower your body forward toward the floor, resisting with your hamstrings and keeping your hips extended.
Lower as far as you can control, then pull yourself back up to the starting position with your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2400.note: Replaced the prone cable curl with the Nordic-style inverse curl, ankles hooked under the pulldown pads.

steps: Strap the arm blaster around your neck so it sits across your stomach, then stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Rest the backs of your upper arms against the arm blaster with your elbows pinned to it.
Exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2401.note: Added the arm blaster setup with the elbows pinned against it.

steps: Strap the arm blaster around your neck and stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso.
Rest the backs of your upper arms against the arm blaster with your elbows pinned to it.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and your palms facing each other, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2402.note: Removed the rotation to palms forward so the grip stays neutral (hammer), and added the arm blaster.

steps: Attach a v-bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Strap the arm blaster around your neck so the plate sits against your lower ribs, and stand facing the machine.
Grasp the v-bar with a neutral or slightly angled grip, thumbs on top, elbows resting against the arm blaster.
Keeping your upper arms still, push the v-bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly, then let the bar rise slowly until your forearms are just above parallel to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2405.note: Added the arm blaster in steps 2 and 4. Revised again after the second review.

steps: Attach an SZ (EZ curl) bar to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Strap the arm blaster around your neck and stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows pinned against the arm blaster and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Engage your triceps and slowly push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2406.note: Changed the straight bar to an SZ bar and added the arm blaster.

steps: Lie flat on your back with the soles of your feet pressed together and your knees dropped out to the sides.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2429.note: Changed step 1 to the frog leg position (soles together, knees out).

steps: Grip a single straight bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart, and jump up to support yourself with your arms locked and the bar in front of your hips.
Bend your knees and cross your ankles, leaning your torso slightly forward.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until the bar is near your chest.
Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2462.note: Changed from parallel bars to a dip on a single straight bar.

steps: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and sit at the pulldown station with your knees under the pads.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with your arms fully extended overhead.
Pull the bar down and toward your right hip in a paddling arc, driving your right elbow down and back and letting the bar tilt.
Return the bar overhead under control.
Pull the bar down toward your left hip in the same paddling arc.
Repeat, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2464.note: Replaced the one-arm low row with the high-pulley bar pulled to alternating hips in a paddling arc.

steps: Kneel on the floor and slide your knees out as wide as is comfortable, with your feet in line with your knees and your toes pointing out.
Lower onto your forearms with your elbows under your shoulders.
Slowly rock your hips back toward your heels until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs.
Pause for a moment, then rock your hips forward to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2571.note: Rewrote as the wide-knee frog stretch rocking the hips back and forth; primary set to adductors.

steps: Adjust the seat of the machine so that your knees are at a 90-degree angle when your feet are on the footplate.
Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and place your right foot in the center of the footplate, keeping your left foot off it.
Place your hands on the handles or sides of the machine for stability.
Push the footplate away from your body by extending your right leg, keeping your back against the backrest.
Pause for a moment at the fully extended position, then slowly bend your leg to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-2611.note: Made the press single-leg in steps 2 and 4.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with one arm out to the side, your upper arm and forearm resting on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell by one end so the weighted end extends past your thumb, with your palm facing up and the weighted end tipped toward the floor.
Keeping your elbow and forearm in place, rotate your forearm inward to lift the weighted end until your thumb points up.
Pause for a moment, then slowly rotate back to the palm-up position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-2705.note: Replaced the prone lift with forearm rotation into pronation, using an off-center dumbbell grip for resistance.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with one arm out to the side, your upper arm and forearm resting on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell by one end so the weighted end extends past your thumb, with your palm facing down and the weighted end tipped toward the floor.
Keeping your elbow and forearm in place, rotate your forearm outward to lift the weighted end until your thumb points up.
Pause for a moment, then slowly rotate back to the palm-down position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-2706.note: Replaced the supine curl with forearm rotation into supination, using an off-center dumbbell grip for resistance.

steps: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your knees under the pads and your feet flat on the ground.
Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing you, about shoulder-width apart.
Sit upright with your chest out and shoulders back, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back.
Pull the handles down towards your chest, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2736.note: Changed step 2 to an underhand, shoulder-width grip.

steps: Stand in front of a step or platform with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.
Place your right foot on the step, ensuring your entire foot is on the surface.
Push through your right heel and step up onto the platform, bringing your left foot up beside it.
Step back down to the floor with your left foot, then your right.
Step your right foot back into a reverse lunge, lowering until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your front heel to bring your right foot back to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the lead leg each time.
yd-2796.note: Added a reverse lunge after each step-up.

yd-2799.name: Barbell Seated Alternate Leg Raise
yd-2799.note: Name typo: Sitted. Revised again after the second review.
steps: Sit on the end of a flat bench with your back straight and hold a light barbell across the front of your shoulders.
Lean back slightly and straighten both legs in front of you, heels on the floor.
Keeping your torso still, raise one straight leg as high as you can.
Lower it under control and raise the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
Stand a short stride in front of a stepbox, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Place the toes of your left foot on the box behind you, keeping most of your weight on your right leg.
Keeping your back straight and core engaged, hinge forward at the hips on your right leg, lowering the dumbbell towards the ground.
Keep your left foot resting lightly on the box as a kickstand throughout the movement.
Lower the dumbbell until you feel a stretch in your right hamstring, then drive your hips forward to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-2805.note: The rear foot now stays on the box as a kickstand instead of lifting off.

steps: Stand in front of a bench or step with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Place your right foot flat on the step, then reach your left foot back so you are in a split stance with your left foot on the floor.
Lower your body by bending both knees, keeping your right foot flat on the step, until your left knee nears the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-2812.note: Replaced the step-up with knee drive with a split squat, front foot on the step.

steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt around your waist, or hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Grab the chin-up bar on the dip cage with a narrow underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended, feet off the ground, and body straight.
Pull your body up, keeping your elbows close to your sides, until your chin is above the bar.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-2987.note: Added load, narrowed the grip, and moved the grip to the cage's chin bar.

steps: Attach the resistance band to a low anchor point behind a chair or bench and loop it around one ankle.
Sit on the chair facing away from the anchor with your knees bent at 90 degrees and your feet flat.
Keeping your thigh still and your upper body stable, straighten your knee against the band until your leg is fully extended.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly bend your knee back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
yd-3007.note: The anchor is now behind you and the movement is knee extension, done seated rather than the flag's standing version.

steps: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Hold the EZ barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms above your chest, then bend your elbows to about 90 degrees so the bar sits above your forehead.
Keeping your elbows fixed at about 90 degrees, lower the barbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch in your lats.
Pause for a moment, then return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the arc motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3010.note: Changed the slight elbow bend to a fixed bend of about 90 degrees.

steps: Place your hands on a bench or elevated surface, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet back, hip-width apart, so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Keeping your elbows locked, let your chest sink toward the bench by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Push through your palms to spread your shoulder blades apart, rounding your upper back slightly.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3011.note: Elbows now stay locked, so only the shoulder blades retract and protract.

steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with your arms straight and your elbows locked.
Keeping your elbows straight, let your shoulders rise toward your ears so your body sinks.
Push your shoulders down away from your ears to lift your body back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3012.note: Rewrote as straight-arm support on dip bars, moving only the shoulder blades (elevation and depression).

steps: Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot flat on the floor, keeping the other leg straight.
Place your hands under your lower back, palms down.
Engaging your abs, lift only your head and shoulder blades a few inches off the floor without bending your neck.
Pause for a moment, then slowly lower back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, switching the bent leg halfway through.
yd-3016.note: Cut the lift down to the head and shoulder blades only, with the hands under the lower back.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell on the floor over your mid-foot.
Bend at the hips and knees until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Row the bar explosively from the floor to your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together without raising your torso.
Lower the bar back to the floor, letting it come to a dead stop.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3017.note: Added the floor start, near-parallel torso, and a dead stop on every rep.

steps: Set a bar at about hip height and place a bench about a body length away from it.
Lie under the bar, grab it with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and rest your heels on the bench.
Hang with your arms fully extended and your body straight from head to heels.
Pull your chest to the bar by squeezing your shoulder blades together and bending your elbows.
Lower yourself back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3019.note: Rewrote as a feet-on-bench inverted row (it had mixed a pull-up and a row).

steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms locked, and your body in a straight line.
Keeping your elbows straight, let your chest sink toward the floor by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Push the floor away to spread your shoulder blades apart, rounding your upper back slightly.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3021.note: Removed the elbow bend so only the shoulder blades move.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Lower your body down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if you were sitting on a chair.
Keep your chest up and your heels on the floor throughout the movement.
Lower yourself into a full-depth squat, with your hips sinking below your knees.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3119.note: Changed to full depth with the heels down; primary set to quadriceps.

steps: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and anchor the middle of the resistance band under the seat or under your feet.
Hold an end of the band in each hand, palms facing forward, at shoulder level.
Press the band overhead, extending your arms fully.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the band back down to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3122.note: Anchored the band under the seat or feet so pressing has resistance.

steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Place the middle of the resistance band under both feet and hold the ends or handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up, arms extended down by your sides.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the band up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower your hands back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3123.note: Anchored the band under both feet in step 2 so the curl has resistance.

steps: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Wrap the resistance band around your upper back (or behind the chair back) and hold a handle in each hand at chest level, palms facing down and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your arms forward, pushing the resistance band away from your chest.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3124.note: Anchored the band behind the upper back/chair in step 2 so the press works against tension.

steps: Stand facing a sturdy vertical post or door frame and grip it at chest height with one hand, your feet close to its base.
Lean back until your arm is fully straight, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest toward your hand, keeping your elbow close to your side and squeezing your shoulder blade back.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back until your arm is straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-3156.note: Replaced the bent-over dumbbell row with a one-arm lean-back row from a fixed anchor, elbow kept close.

steps: Stand facing a sturdy fixed bar or door frame and grip it with both hands close together at chest height.
Walk your feet in toward the anchor and lean back until your arms are fully straight, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows close to your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back until your arms are straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3158.note: Replaced the unloaded bent-over pull with a close-grip lean-back row from a fixed anchor.

steps: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or door handle and hold both ends of the towel in one hand, standing with your feet close to the anchor.
Lean back until your arm is fully straight, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest toward your hand, squeezing your shoulder blade back.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back until your arm is straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
yd-3161.note: Anchored the towel to a fixed post and changed the forward hinge to a one-arm lean-back row.

steps: Stand facing a sturdy post or door frame and grip it at chest height with one hand, your feet close to its base.
Lean back until your arm is fully extended, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your body toward your hand, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower yourself back until your arm is straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-3162.note: Replaced the dumbbell row with a one-arm lean-back row from a fixed anchor.

steps: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or door handle and hold one end in each hand, standing with your feet close to the anchor.
Lean back until your arms are fully straight, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest toward your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back until your arms are straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3165.note: Anchored the towel to a fixed post and replaced the forward hinge with a lean-back row.

steps: Stand facing a sturdy fixed bar or frame at chest height and grasp it with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Walk your feet in toward the anchor and lean back until your arms are straight, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Pull your chest toward the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower yourself back until your arms are straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3166.note: Added the fixed anchor and backward lean so the row moves the body against bodyweight.

steps: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or door handle and hold one end in each hand, palms facing down, feet shoulder-width apart close to the anchor.
Sit back into a squat, leaning away from the anchor until your arms are fully straight, with your back straight and chest up.
Pull your chest toward your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades together, as you drive up out of the squat to standing.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly extend your arms and sit back down into the squat.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3167.note: Anchored the towel to a post and timed the row with rising out of the squat, as in the non-towel squatting row.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding onto a sturdy object or suspension trainer with your arms extended.
Lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight, heels down and torso braced, letting your knees track over your toes.
From the squat position, pull your body up towards the object or suspension trainer, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3168.note: Replaced only the outdated knees-behind-toes cue in step 2.

steps: Adjust the machine to fit your body and lie face down with the lever pad just above your ankles and your knees just off the edge of the bench.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine for support.
Keeping your hips pressed into the bench, curl the pad up toward your glutes with both legs.
At the top, take one leg off the pad and slowly lower the weight with the other leg alone.
Curl the pad back up with both legs, then lower it with the opposite leg.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the lowering leg.
yd-3195.note: Changed the seated setup to lying prone and added the two-legs-up, one-leg-down pattern.

steps: Stand on the platform of the lever row machine, hinge at the hips and rest your chest on the pad if there is one, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the V-bar with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, arms fully extended.
Pull the V-bar towards your abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3200.note: Replaced the seat cue with a bent-over stance and fixed the grip to neutral on the V-bar.

steps: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, curl your head and shoulders up only until your shoulder blades clear the floor, about a quarter of the full sit-up range.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3201.note: Shortened the range in step 3 to a quarter sit-up (shoulder blades just clearing the floor).

steps: Start by kneeling on the ground with your hands shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Walk your hands forward and keep your knees on the floor so your body forms a straight line from your knees to your head.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Continue lowering until your chest is just above the ground, then push back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3211.note: Step 2 now keeps the knees down (straight line knees to head) instead of a full push-up.

steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides.
Keeping your arms apart and your legs straight, rotate your torso and bend down to bring your right hand toward your left foot.
Sweep your torso and arms in a circle across your body and back up through the starting position.
Repeat the circle the other way, bringing your left hand toward your right foot, with both feet staying planted.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3214.note: Replaced the single-leg hinge with a wide-stance rotating toe touch that circles back up; feet stay planted.

steps: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, interlace your fingers, turn your palms away from you and extend your arms overhead.
Keeping your hands clasped and arms straight, bend to one side and circle your torso down toward the toes of that foot.
Continue the circle, sweeping your clasped hands across past the toes of the other foot.
Rise up the opposite side to return your arms overhead.
Repeat the circle in the opposite direction.
Continue alternating directions for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3215.note: Rewrote the incoherent sequence: palms-out clasped hands overhead circle down past the toes and back up, alternating direction.

steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Push yourself back up to the high plank.
At the top, lift your right hand and tap your left chest, then return it to the floor.
Perform another push-up, then tap your right chest with your left hand.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3216.note: Moved the chest tap to the top plank so both hands are down during the push-up.

steps: Start in a downward dog position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, feet hip-width apart and hips high in an inverted V.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down and forward close to the ground, between your hands.
Continue forward, straightening your arms and lifting your chest into an upward dog with your hips low.
Push your hips back and up to return to the downward dog position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3217.note: Reordered into the real Hindu push-up flow: down dog, swoop through to up dog, push back to down dog.

steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your body only about halfway down, as if beginning to sit back into a chair.
Keep your chest up and your weight in your heels.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3221.note: Limited depth to half range in step 2; primary changed from cardio to quadriceps.

steps: Set a cable handle at chest height and kneel on a pad facing away from the machine, with your ankles secured under a fixed pad or held by a partner.
Hold the cable handle against your chest with both hands so the cable pulls back against you, and keep your body straight from knees to head.
Keeping your hips extended, slowly lower your torso forward toward the floor by straightening your knees, letting the cable assist you.
Lower as far as you can control, then curl your body back up to upright by pulling with your hamstrings.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3235.note: Replaced the prone leg curl with a cable-assisted Nordic (inverse) curl from kneeling with ankles anchored.

steps: Kneel tall on the ground with your knees hip-width apart.
Wrap the resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Place your hands on your hips or extend them out in front of you for balance.
Sit your hips back toward your heels, keeping your chest up.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to upright kneeling, keeping your knees on the floor and pushing them out against the band.
Hold the position for a moment, then sit your hips back again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3236.note: Removed the impossible knee lift; hips now sit back to the heels and drive forward with the knees down.

steps: Place one end of a barbell in a landmine and stand side-on to it with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold the free end of the bar in the hand farthest from the anchor, arm hanging down in front of your hips.
Keeping your core engaged and a slight bend in your elbow, raise the bar out to the side up to shoulder height.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-3237.note: Added the landmine setup and rewrote as a one-arm lateral raise to shoulder height.

steps: Start in a kneeling position with your hands on the ground, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your hands forward and keep your knees on the floor so your body forms a straight line from your knees to your head.
Keeping your core engaged and your hips stable, lift one hand off the ground and tap the opposite shoulder.
Return the hand to the ground and repeat with the other hand.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3239.note: Step 2 now keeps the knees down instead of moving into a full plank.

steps: Stand with your back to a wall and your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place an exercise ball between the wall and your lower back.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms extended by your sides.
Place a tennis ball between your ankles.
Raise your heels off the ground, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3241.note: Step 1 now has your back to the wall, matching the ball placement.

steps: Set the Smith machine bar at about shoulder height.
Step under the bar and position it across your upper back, resting on your traps.
Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out, then stand up and rotate the bar to unhook it.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, initiate the squat by bending your knees and hips.
Lower your body as deep as your mobility allows, hips well below your knees, keeping your back neutral.
Drive through your feet to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3281.note: Removed the step back (Smith bar is unhooked by rotating) and took the depth to a full squat below parallel.

steps: Put on a weight vest or a dip belt with weight attached, then hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull explosively, driving the bar toward your lower chest.
As you reach the bar, quickly roll your wrists over it and bring your chest over the top of the bar.
Press down until your arms are straight and you are supported above the bar.
Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting hang, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3286.note: Added the load and replaced the grip-switch chest-to-bar pull with an actual transition over the bar and press to support.

steps: Stand with your back to a straight bar at hip height and grip it behind you with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Jump or press up into support on straight arms, with the bar behind your hips and your legs extended in front of you.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, letting your shoulders extend and your hips move forward until the bar is near your upper back.
Pause for a moment, then press back up to straight arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3288.note: Replaced the parallel-bar dip with the Korean dip on a single straight bar held behind the body.

steps: Position yourself between two parallel bars with your arms fully extended and your body suspended in the air.
Bend your knees and cross your ankles.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your forearms rest along the bars.
Pause for a moment, then press through your hands to lift your forearms off the bars and straighten your arms without kicking.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3289.note: Lowered to forearms on the bars and pressed back up from there, which defines the impossible dip.

steps: Put on a weight vest or a dip belt with weight attached.
Grab the pull-up bar with one hand using an overhand grip, letting your other arm hang free or holding your working wrist.
Hang from the bar with your arm fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar by bending your elbow and squeezing your back muscles.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Lower your body back down to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
yd-3290.note: Made it one-handed and added the load.

steps: Sit on the floor in a wide straddle with your legs straight and your hands on the floor between your legs, close to your hips.
Lock your elbows and lean your shoulders forward over your hands.
Press down through your hands to lift your hips and legs off the floor, keeping the legs straight and straddled.
Continue lifting your hips up over your hands until they are stacked over your shoulders, then bring your legs up into a handstand.
Lower back down the same way under control to the straddle sit.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3291.note: Replaced the squat with the straddle-sit press to handstand; primary changed to shoulders since it is a straight-arm press.

steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands placed very wide, both on the floor, fingers pointing out slightly.
Shift your weight toward your right hand and lower your body toward it, bending only your right elbow.
Keep your left arm straight as it slides or extends out to the side, and keep your back straight and core engaged.
Press back up through your right hand to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, lowering toward your left hand with your right arm straight.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3294.note: Kept both hands on the floor and made only one elbow bend while the other arm stays straight.

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, palms facing away from you.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Keeping your arms straight and your body straight, pull the bar down toward your hips to raise your whole body up to horizontal, face up.
Slowly lower your body back down to the hang under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3295.note: Changed the leg raise and timed hold into straight-arm whole-body raises to horizontal for reps; primary lats for consistency with yd-3296.

steps: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the bar down toward your hips to raise your body up, tucking your knees first if needed.
Extend your hips and legs so your whole body is straight and horizontal, face up.
Hold this position for the desired time.
To release, slowly lower your body back down to the hang.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3296.note: Replaced the L-hang with a straight-arm horizontal hold; primary changed to lats, abdominals moved to secondary.

steps: Hang from a pull-up bar or rings with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Tuck your knees and rotate backward, bringing your legs up between your arms until your body is upside down, hips over shoulders.
Extend your legs straight up into an inverted hang, arms straight and body in one line.
Keeping your arms locked, slowly lower your body backward, away from the bar, until it is horizontal and face down.
Hold the horizontal position with your body straight and glutes tight, tucking your knees if you need an easier version.
Raise back to the inverted hang, then tuck and rotate back down to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3297.note: Replaced the front-facing leg raise with the skin-the-cat entry into a horizontal face-down hold with arms behind the body. Revised again after the second review.

steps: Place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers turned out slightly, with your feet spread wide behind you.
Lock your elbows and push the floor away to round your upper back slightly.
Lean your shoulders forward past your hands until your feet lift off the floor, keeping your legs straight and straddled.
Hold your body horizontal on straight arms for the desired time.
Lower your feet back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3298.note: Replaced the wide-feet push-up with a straight-arm straddle planche hold; primary shoulders, consistent with yd-3299.

yd-3299.note: Agreed with the metadata flag; steps already describe the hold and are kept. Revised again after the second review.
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart, fingers turned slightly out, and your feet together.
Lock your elbows, push the floor away so your shoulder blades spread apart, and brace your core and glutes.
Lean your shoulders forward past your hands until your feet become light, then lift them off the floor.
Keep leaning until your whole body is straight and parallel to the floor, legs together, balancing on your hands.
Hold the position with straight arms for the desired time.
Lower your feet back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Start in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your body straight.
Engage your core and slowly shift your weight forward, bringing your shoulders past your hands.
Keep your elbows locked, your shoulders pushed away from the floor and your body straight as you lean forward.
Hold this position for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3300.note: Step 3 now has locked elbows and protracted shoulders; primary changed to shoulders.

steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers spread.
Bend your elbows slightly and rest your knees on the outside of your upper arms, just above the elbows.
Lean forward, shifting your weight onto your hands until your feet lift off the floor.
Hold the balance for the desired time.
Lower your feet back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3301.note: Added the defining knees-on-elbows lean-forward balance; primary changed to shoulders.

steps: Stand facing a wall about a step away from it.
Place your hands on the ground shoulder-width apart, a hand's length from the wall, fingers pointing forward.
Kick your legs up so your heels rest against the wall, using your core and shoulders to maintain balance.
Once in a handstand position, lock your arms and push the floor away to support your body weight.
Hold the handstand for the desired time.
To come down, slowly lower your legs back to the ground one at a time.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3302.note: Made it wall-supported from step 1 to match the kick to the wall; primary changed to shoulders.

steps: Stand side-on to a sturdy vertical pole and grip it with both hands, the top hand above your head and the bottom hand about shoulder-width below it.
Lock your bottom arm straight and push it into the pole while pulling with your top arm.
Engage your core and lift your feet off the ground, raising your body sideways.
Bring your body to horizontal with your legs straight and together, side-on to the pole.
Hold this position for the desired time, then lower your legs back down to the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
yd-3303.note: Replaced the pole leg raise with the human flag: hands stacked, top arm pulling, bottom arm pushing, body horizontal side-on.

steps: Put on a weight vest or a dip belt with weight attached, then hang from a pull-up bar with a false or overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Swing slightly or brace, then pull explosively, driving the bar toward your lower chest.
As your chest reaches the bar, lean forward and turn your wrists over so your hands are on top of the bar.
Press down on the bar until your arms are straight and you are supported above it.
Lower yourself under control back through the transition to a hang.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3312.note: Added the weight vest/belt to step 1; the rest was already right. Revised again after the second review.

steps: Put on a dip belt with weight attached and grip a single straight bar in front of you with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Jump up into support with your arms straight and the bar in front of your hips.
Lean slightly forward over the bar and lower your body by bending your elbows until the bar is near your chest.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
yd-3313.note: Moved from parallel bars to a single straight bar in front of the body and added the load.
